6553bbf6ac4a9615: ALOR STAR: Bukit Aman will hold discussions with Pakistani authorities on the next course of action following the detention of 130 Malaysians suspected of involvement in a cybercrime syndicate.

Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said he had directed the Bukit Aman Commercial Crime Investigation Department (CCID) director to meet the relevant Pakistani authorities to discuss the matter.
He said the directive followed a telephone call from his Pakistani counterpart about the arrests, which took place about two weeks ago.
"I have asked the Bukit Aman CCID director to meet and discuss the matter with the relevant department in Pakistan to determine how we should handle this issue.

"Discussions are underway, and I will receive a report before deciding on the next course of action," he said after attending a special financial assistance handover ceremony for taxi, rental car and school bus drivers at Dewan Insaniah, Lembaga Zakat Negeri Kedah (LZNK) Complex, Mergong, here today.
Saifuddin said a previous police operation at Kulim Hi-Tech Park had also led to the arrest of 33 Pakistanis and several Indians suspected of involvement in similar activities.
He said the Pakistanis detained during the operation had been charged in court.
Last week, Pakistani authorities arrested 130 Malaysians in a raid on an online scam centre in Rawalpindi.
Pakistan news portal ProPakistani had reported that the scam centre targeted Malaysians.

Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail had said the matter had been referred to the Commercial Crime Investigation Department (CCID) director following the detention of 130 Malaysians in the raid.

42bbc7bcd4b65505: PEKAN: Universiti Malaysia Pahang Al-Sultan Abdullah's (UMPSA) Centre for Modern Languages has been elevated to the Faculty of Applied Language Studies to meet industry needs.

UMPSA vice-chancellor Professor Ts Dr Yatimah Alias said the change would enrich students' learning experience and widen access for the community and industry to language education, training and skills development.
She said the move reflected the university's efforts to broaden its academic focus beyond technology and engineering while producing graduates with strong communication skills.
"This initiative reflects our commitment to broadening academic excellence by emphasising language skills that are dynamic and relevant to current needs.
"In the digital economy, language proficiency and communication skills are essential for individuals to interact, share expertise and compete internationally," she said in a statement.

Yatimah said UMPSA's strengths in technology, engineering and Advanced Technical and Vocational Education and Training provided a strategic platform to expand applied language studies by integrating communication skills with technical knowledge.
Faculty of Applied Language Studies dean Associate Professor Dr Zuraina Ali said the faculty would develop new programmes and collaborate with industry players.
She said this included offering a Master of Science in Technology-Integrated Language Learning through Open and Distance Learning.
UMPSA was established as Kolej Universiti Kejuruteraan dan Teknologi Malaysia on Feb 16, 2002, as the country's 16th higher learning institution.
f21805418f44aa5e: WASHINGTON: Democrats teed up final get-out-the-vote rallies Monday on the eve of midterm elections where they expect to win at least partial control of Congress and impose political constraints on President Donald Trump for the first time in two years.
Rallies – including by star Democratic Senate candidates James Talarico in Texas and Adam Hamilton in Kansas – were capping a campaign of breathtaking tension and bitterness.

For his closing argument, Trump chose a speech in Washington at the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool – a landmark that has become synonymous with the 80-year-old president's obsessive, controversial drive to redevelop the US capital.
"We're going to win," he said on Sunday.
Polls, however, show that Democrats are near certain to take the majority from Republicans in the House of Representatives and have a real shot at winning the currently Republican Senate.

Even winning just the House would mean Democrats have voting power over the federal budget and would lead powerful committees able to investigate alleged corruption under Trump, the Epstein files and other explosive issues.

The loss of total Republican dominance would push Trump into unfamiliar and uncomfortable territory: a lame-duck period beset with high inflation at home, the sputtering war against Iran and hostile Democratic investigations into his activities in Washington.
But a decade into the Trump era, Democrats remain wary about predictions of victory.
"Nauseously optimistic," Democratic Senator Raphael Warnock told CNN to describe the mood.

Republicans led by Trump have fought a political scorched-earth campaign, painting Democrats as communists and openly branding Abdul El-Sayed, a Muslim candidate for senator in Michigan, as a terrorist.
Addressing a crowd in Iowa on Sunday, Trump said Democrats are "extreme and dangerous radicals" who will "steal your wealth" and let in migrants to "ransack, rape and plunder."
But polls show Americans heavily souring on Trump's wrecking-ball act.
An NBC News poll released on Sunday showed 60 per cent disapprove of his performance, particularly over high prices exacerbated by his now eight-month war against Iran.
While the House seems highly likely to turn Democratic, the battle for the Senate is up in the air.
Only a third of the Senate's 100 seats are being contested in these midterms, and few of the races were seen as favourable to Democrats.
However, with surprisingly strong challenges in deeply Republican states, pollsters now say the odds of a Democratic flip are at minimum even.
The final New York Times/Siena poll released Sunday evening showed Democratic candidates leading in all seven seats viewed as most competitive, though five remained within the margin of error.
A Democratic Senate would be able to shut down Trump's lifetime appointments to courts – especially the Supreme Court.
While Tuesday is election day, early voting has already seen a record 54 million people cast ballots around the country.
The midterms have seen about US$11 billion spent on advertising, with large chunks coming from individual mega-donors.
Elon Musk, a close Trump ally who led the so-called DOGE effort in dismantling entire government departments, has given a staggering nearly half-billion dollars to help get Republicans elected.

7ea56020811171fc: PETALING JAYA: Malaysia has a strategic advantage ahead of Asean's next digital leap through its two 5G networks, which are anchored to different technological ecosystems.
However, analysts warn that possible or potential procurement decisions could erode this advantage without explicit safeguards.

Under the dual-network framework, Digital Nasional Bhd (DNB) has deployed Sweden's Ericsson technology, while U Mobile's upcoming second network will rely on Chinese telecommunications giants Huawei and ZTE.
This gives Malaysia an uncommon operational bridge between Western- and China-linked technological spheres.

National Defence University of Malaysia (UPNM) academic Khairol Amali Ahmad said this technological divide was pivotal. Multinational corporations entering Asean increasingly face stringent internal cybersecurity requirements, vendor restrictions and regulatory conditions.
"Having two distinct 5G technology ecosystems could provide a strategic advantage for Malaysia as a digital hub of Southeast Asia," he said.

He said the arrangement allowed Malaysia to cater to American, European and Japanese enterprises with specific compliance requirements, as well as businesses already integrated into Chinese technology ecosystems.
Khairol added that maintaining both options would reduce over-reliance on a single supply chain amid shifting geopolitical dynamics.
He said this also reflected Malaysia's non-aligned foreign policy as tensions between the United States and China affected regional trade, technology and capital flows.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has championed the dual-network strategy as a pragmatic approach to ensuring the country retains access to both Western and Eastern innovation.
SAFEGUARDS AMID OWNERSHIP TRANSITION
Khairol stressed that the strategic advantage depended on both networks remaining technologically distinct, a position that could be vulnerable to commercial changes.

On Oct 1, DNB announced preparations to transition to equal equity ownership among CelcomDigi, Maxis Broadband and YTL Power International, following the withdrawal of Minister of Finance Inc (MOF Inc) as an ordinary shareholder.
MOF Inc will retain a special golden share to safeguard strategic national interests.

Khairol cautioned that the commercial priorities of private shareholders could influence future infrastructure contracts, potentially diluting the distinction between the networks' underlying technologies.

"Without explicit safeguards, routine contract renewals, system upgrades and hardware replacement cycles could gradually leave Malaysia with two networks that are no longer meaningfully different in their underlying technology," he said.
He said the authorities should clarify whether preserving distinct technological ecosystems fell within the mandate of MOF Inc's special share and the sector's regulatory framework.
"Without formal protection, Malaysia risks losing the unique strategic advantage it gained by pivoting from a Single Wholesale Network (SWN) to a dual-network model," Khairol said.
He added that explicit statutory commitments would provide greater certainty for foreign investors.
PRESERVING INVESTOR CONFIDENCE

Echoing the concern, Global Asia Consulting analyst Samirul Ariff Othman warned that removing distinct technology options relied on by security-conscious enterprises could trigger compliance concerns and undermine investor confidence.

"If technology changes removed the option relied upon by security-sensitive customers, my assessment is that Malaysia could face stronger diplomatic scrutiny, additional corporate compliance checks and demands for dedicated connectivity," Samirul said.

"Some investment decisions could become slower or more costly. There would also be a credibility issue if Malaysia first promised enduring separation and subsequently diluted it without consultation," he added.

Khairol said retaining both networks should be positioned not as an effort to exclude Chinese technology, but as a commitment to investor choice, technological sovereignty and supply-chain resilience.
Samirul added that the benchmark for success lay in operational verification.

"Any assurance must also define what 'Western-only' covers and how compliance would be verified. Sharing passive physical infrastructure is a very different proposition from sharing sensitive network functions, core operational control or privileged data access," he said.
ASEAN DIGITAL DIVIDEND

The policy crossroads comes as Asean works towards concluding the Digital Economy Framework Agreement (Defa), which is projected to accelerate the regional digital economy towards US$2 trillion (RM8.6 trillion) by 2030.
Defa aims to harmonise digital trade, cross-border data governance and digital payments, alongside emerging areas such as artificial intelligence.
Khairol said preserving two distinct technological options would help Malaysia secure a significant share of that growth.

"The ultimate advantage lies not merely in having two distinct networks on paper, but in preserving the genuine technological diversity that makes Malaysia an indispensable destination for multinational investment across both hemispheres," he said.

f680de970fa7c679: KUALA LUMPUR: A 58-member Chinese business delegation has indicated potential investments worth about US$15 billion in Malaysia, says Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.
He said he had been working for some time to bring the investors to Samalaju in Bintulu, Sarawak, to produce aluminium for the international market.
"The Malaysian market is too small," he said at a press conference after meeting the delegation today.

Zahid, who is also rural and regional development minister, said the investors planned to build not only manufacturing plants but also green energy facilities to generate electricity for their operations.
"In my view, this can really help Sarawak," he said, adding that he had discussed the matter with caretaker Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg and several senior figures in the state.
"They chose Malaysia because they know that Malaysia has great potential in terms of investment," he said, adding that he knew most of the investors and that they were "more confident in us now."
He said the investors had chosen Malaysia because they recognised its investment potential.
He said the investors wanted to expand their operations in Malaysia in the same sectors in which they were involved in China
"After this, I will facilitate business matching with their prospective partners," he said.
He added that government officials had briefed the delegation on Malaysia's investment climate and available incentives.

The delegation was focusing on six sectors: electrical and electronics (E&E) and semiconductors; specialised industrial materials and precision engineering; digital economy and technology infrastructure; food processing and halal products; health technology; and tourism.
"They know that Malaysia's position in electrical and electronics and semiconductors is very significant," he said.
On data centres, Zahid said Malaysia already had many such facilities.
"However, if they are keen, it is better for them to work with existing companies, either jointly or by taking over," he said.
On halal food processing, he said China's largest dairy producer, which already had a presence in Malaysia, was keen to expand its operations.
"They intend to share their technology with us and also expand investment in processing, especially dairy products," he said.
He said health technology companies were interested in obtaining halal certification in Malaysia.
"They want to manufacture those health products in our country for export," he said.
"Their products have received approval from the FDA (Food and Drug Administration), but they do not have halal certification," he added.
Zahid said Malaysia's halal certification had been recognised worldwide for 52 years, making products certified here more readily accepted in Middle Eastern and American markets.
"So they want to use not only the certification but also the environment and investment climate in Malaysia, which is more conducive," he said.
In tourism, he said the investors were looking at developing resorts and hotels, with some also seeking halal certification, including a company affiliated with a global hotel network.
Asked what Malaysia hoped to gain from China, Zahid said the government was prioritising high-value investments.
"We are now focusing on high-value investment, meaning high-end. No longer labour-intensive," he said, adding that most of the proposed investments involved automation.
"In my view, this is something good compared with previous investments," he said.
China is Malaysia's largest trading partner for 17 consecutive years, with bilateral trade reaching about US$126.8 billion in 2025.
Zahid made a five-day working visit to China from Oct 12 to 16 to strengthen bilateral ties in trade, investment, technology and technical and vocational education and training (TVET).

700d2778eca4ac01: KUALA LUMPUR: The Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC) has objected to a bid by Teoh Beng Hock's family for leave to initiate a judicial review to compel police to investigate his death as murder.
The judicial review application was filed by the late political aide's brother, Teoh Meng Kee, and their parents, Teoh Leong Hwee and Teng Shuw Hoi.
They named the Inspector-General of Police, the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) director, the police, the Attorney-General, and the Malaysian government as the first to fifth respondents.
Federal Counsel Mohammad Salehuddin Md Ali, representing all respondents, argued that the applicants failed to file their application within the prescribed period.
He said the application filed by the family on April 17 did not comply with the three-month statutory deadline under Order 53 Rule 3(6) of the Rules of Court 2012.

Salehuddin argued that the family had known since June 28, 2019, that police investigations were classified under Section 342 of the Penal Code for wrongful confinement, rather than Section 302 for murder or Section 304 for culpable homicide not amounting to murder.

He said this was evident in a letter sent by the family's former counsel, Karpal Singh & Company, to the A-GC on June 28, 2019, raising the disparity between the investigation classification and the Court of Appeal's 2014 findings.
"This is a challenge against the authorities' failure to act, and the relief sought is an order of mandamus to compel that action.

"Therefore, the applicable time frame is three months from the date the grounds of the application first arose, not from the date the decision was communicated to the applicants," he said before High Court judge Norliza Othman.
Salehuddin said that based on the family's knowledge on June 28, 2019, the three-month window to file the application expired on Sept 29, 2019.
He said filing the application on April 17 resulted in a delay of roughly six years and six months.

"The family's reason that they only obtained clear confirmation regarding the investigation's classification through the Selangor police chief's letter dated Jan 20 cannot be accepted because the matter had already been raised much earlier," he said.
He said grounds of public interest and the absence of prejudice to the respondents — given that investigation records were still intact — were insufficient to justify the delay.
Salehuddin said the applicants must demonstrate good reasons to obtain an extension of time under Order 53 Rule 3(7) of the Rules of Court 2012.

However, counsel for the family, Lim Wei Jiet, argued that the applicants only obtained clear confirmation that police were not investigating the case under Section 302 or Section 304 through the Selangor police chief's letter dated Jan 20.
He said the application filed on April 17 was within three months of that date.
After hearing submissions from both parties, judge Norliza fixed Nov 17 to deliver her decision on the A-GC's preliminary objection.

In their application, the family is seeking a declaration that all respondents have a legal duty to initiate an investigation into Beng Hock's death on July 16, 2009, under Section 302 of the Penal Code for murder or Section 304 for culpable homicide not amounting to murder.
They are also seeking an order of mandamus directing the respondents to complete the investigation within 120 days from the date of the order.
On Nov 21, 2024, the High Court ordered the police to complete the investigation into Beng Hock's death within six months after granting a judicial review application by his parents.

However, on May 20, 2025, the Selangor police contingent headquarters CID informed the family's former solicitors by letter that the case was being investigated for wrongful confinement under Section 342 of the Penal Code.
[2/11/2026 3:21 PM] Sharm: The letter also stated that the A-GC decided there would be no further action on the matter.

Beng Hock, then political secretary to Seri Kembangan assemblyman Ean Yong Hian Wah, was found dead on July 16, 2009, at Plaza Masalam in Shah Alam after giving a statement at the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission office on the 14th floor.
On Jan 5, 2011, the Shah Alam Coroner's Court returned an open verdict, ruling that Beng Hock's death was neither suicide nor homicide, with no third-party involvement.
However, on July 21, 2011, a Royal Commission of Inquiry formed to investigate the case ruled that his death was a suicide.
On Sept 5, 2014, the Court of Appeal set aside the open verdict, ruling that Beng Hock's death was caused by an unlawful act by one or more unknown individuals.

0bcd54b5cef9c5b8: Welcome to Monday morning, an occasion The Register marks with a new instalment of "Who, Me?" It's our reader-contributed column in which you confess to workplace mistakes and share your escapes from subsequent scrapes.
This week, meet a reader we'll Regomize as "Gordon" who told us he once worked as an engineer at a major semiconductor corporation.

Gordon rose to become manager of an engineering team which worked on a very popular PC chipset. One of the chaps on this team wasn't pulling his weight, so Gordon got the job of telling him to improve, or leave.
"In all fairness, he was a nice guy but not a great engineer and needed to be better," Gordon told The Register.

Not long after that moment of managerial unpleasantness, Gordon's team got the job of doing a full backup of the chipset's "production stepping" – the silicon equivalent of a minor point release. The idea was to create a detailed record that could be used as a restore point.

"This was not a nightly backup, but a purposeful backup to retain a snapshot of the entire cleaned-up design database for future cases where we might need to spin another stepping quickly," Gordon explained.
Gordon told his underperforming colleague to do the backup. "Because I was overworked, I did not think this through," he told The Register.
The at-risk worker quickly proved why he was under the pump by deciding the backup wasn't necessary until the team completed the next stepping – but didn't tell anyone about that plan.
Before that next stepping was done, the employee's past indiscretions caught up with him and he was let go.
The story now fast-forwards six years, to a moment when Gordon learned that a customer wanted to buy the old chipset design so they could make a radiation-hardened version to use on satellites.
The major semiconductor company liked the sound of that, and asked Gordon to find the backup.

"My colleague and I then pieced together what had happened," he wrote. "Being good engineers, we said nothing. We searched through old nightly backup tapes until we found bits and pieces of different steppings of the design database and copied them all to one place, then handed this off to the customer."
To this day, Gordon doesn't know if the customer was able to produce a useful chip from the bits of backup he cobbled together.
"Did they realize they received bits and pieces of two slightly different databases? Did they care? Was the project canceled before anyone realized it?"

"From then on, I was more careful about who I assigned the task of creating restore backups for each design project," he told The Register. "And I kept a record of the emails requesting backups and confirmation that backups had been done."
Have you given a job to the wrong person? Or given clients slightly dodgy data? In either case, click here to send email to Who, Me? We would love to tell your tale on a future Monday. ®
06c0372dd4846e56: MUAR: A 34-year-old welder was sentenced to six years in jail and two strokes of the rotan after pleading guilty to raping a Form Two student in a forested area in Tangkak last month.
Herwan Abdul Rani pleaded guilty when the charge was read out before Sessions Court judge Emelia Kaswati Mohamad Khalid here.
The court also ordered him to be placed under police supervision for a year after completing his prison sentence.
He was charged with raping the underage girl in a forested area near Taman Kesang Bayu, Tangkak, between midnight and 1.30am on Oct 23.
The offence under Section 376(1) of the Penal Code carries a jail term of up to 20 years and whipping upon conviction.
The girl's mother had lodged a police report, claiming that her daughter had been raped by a man she knew.
Investigations revealed that the victim and the accused had known each other for about a month.
On the night of the incident, the girl told her mother she was going out to attend a silat lesson near their home.
However, the mother later woke up to find her daughter missing and sought police assistance to locate her.
The girl was found emerging from a forested area near an oil palm plantation.
When questioned by her mother, she said that she was raped.
b14b810460523c30: KUALA LUMPUR: Zulfahmi Khairuddin believes his charge Hakim Danish Ramli needs to forget about the Moto3 Rookie of the Year standings and just take things one race at time.
Danish finished third at Mugello and won at Brno, both in July, before suffering a mid-season slump in form.
But the Aeon Credit-MT Helmets-MSI rider came back strong at the Petronas Grand Prix of Malaysia over the weekend, qualifying third and finishing fourth in the lightweight class race.
Zulfahmi, who has been mentoring and managing Danish since 2020, said Danish's focus was much better at Sepang.
"I believe now is the time for us to focus on taking things one race at a time rather than thinking too much about the championship, which put too much pressure on him," said Zulfahmi yesterday.
"When we take things one race at a time, like we did here at Sepang, he is much more focused and the results show that.
"When he is thinking too much about Veda Pratama or Brian Uriarte, he loses that focus.
"If he can just focus on one race at a time, at the end of the day the points will show where he is at."
Zulfahmi added that Danish, 19, has had a steep learning curve to overcome since stepping up to Moto3 this season.
"We all know that Danish has immense potential but as a rookie, it is very difficult to be consistent," he said.
"There are tracks that he has never raced at and then there are also tracks which he is familiar with but is suddenly struggling to find pace on.
"There are a lot of challenges and so we have to manage our expectations.
"Having said that, the team is genuinely happy with Danish this season.
"I believe Danish still has a lot more room for improvement and there is also room to improve his bike."
Danish is currently ninth in the overall Moto3 standings on 116 points.
Veda (Honda Team Asia) is seventh on 131 points while Uriarte (Red Bull KTM Ajo) is third (205 points) in the standings.
The duo, who were both Danish's rivals in the Red Bull Rookies Cup last year, are again his rivals in the Moto3 Rookie of the Year class this season.
Danish will next race at the Qatar GP which is scheduled to start on Friday.

e2618c1faecb24f8: TUMPAT: Three Malaysians and a Thai have been arrested for their alleged involvement in smuggling and illegal entry activities along the Kelantan-Thailand border.
The arrests followed drone surveillance by the General Operations Force (GOF).
GOF Southeast Brigade commander Datuk Ahmad Radzi Hussain said the arrests were made during four separate operations between Oct 10 and 16.
He said three suspects were arrested in Rantau Panjang, while another was detained in Pengkalan Kubor, Tumpat.
The operations also led to the seizure of vehicles, contraband cigarettes, ketum juice and Thai food products worth RM168,800.
"Besides conducting routine patrols, GOF personnel also deployed drones during Op Taring Wawasan Kelantan (OTWK) along the country's border with Thailand.
"Through the operations last month, we managed to arrest four people, including a Thai woman.
"The woman was arrested on Oct 10 for entering Malaysia through an illegal jetty in Pengkalan Kubor," he said.
He was speaking to reporters after witnessing the handover of OTWK from the Ninth Battalion to the Seventh Battalion here today.
Radzi said two Malaysian men were arrested at Jalan Lubok Stol, Rantau Panjang, on Oct 14.
A motorcycle and 1.5 litres of ketum juice were seized during the operation, with the total value of the seizures estimated at RM5,000.
"Another operation on Oct 16 at Kampung Bonggol Kulim, also in Rantau Panjang, resulted in the seizure of a Proton Saga and 60,000 sticks of white cigarettes worth RM152,200.
"However, no arrests were made during the operation," he said.
In the final operation, also conducted on Oct 16, a Malaysian man was arrested for allegedly smuggling 32 packets of Thai snacks.
"A Perodua Kancil was also seized during the operation at an illegal jetty in Kedap.
"The vehicle and food products were valued at RM11,600," he added.
Radzi said the operations demonstrated the effectiveness of drone technology in strengthening border surveillance and curbing smuggling activities along the Golok River.
Separately, he said the Southeast Brigade had recorded 1,493 smuggling cases as of Nov 1, with seized goods valued at more than RM82.5 million.
During the same period, 1,733 people, mostly smugglers, were arrested.

a16dea2ee6d79c97: SHANGHAI: China's central bank injected cash into the banking system on Monday, as it formally shifted its main policy rate to an overnight lending rate, a move analysts said would ease funding costs and support the economy.
The People's Bank of China (PBOC) injected 541 billion yuan (US$81.3 billion) through overnight reverse repurchase agreements at 1.25 per cent, according to a statement.
The central bank said last Friday that it would start to conduct overnight reverse repos every day and switch the seven-day operations to multiple rates from a single fixed one.

"The policy rate has officially shifted its anchor to the overnight rate, with the 1.25 per cent pricing confirming the existing benchmark for funding costs," said Ming Ming, chief economist at CITIC Securities.
Analysts said the change effectively lowers the floor of China's interest-rate framework by 15 basis points, reducing borrowing costs for financial institutions.
Although the move was not a conventional policy rate cut, it would help lower yields across the bond curve, they added.
"Judging by the initial 1.25 per cent rate, the monetary policy stance is steering short-term interest rates downward," said Marco Sun, chief financial market analyst at MUFG (China).
The shift comes as credit concerns from state-owned developer Zhuhai Huafa Group have unsettled the bond market and added pressure on policymakers to shore up investor confidence.
Zhaopeng Xing, senior China strategist at ANZ, said the move was equivalent to a targeted 15-basis-point rate cut for financial institutions.
"It's effectively a red packet for financial institutions, boosting their net interest margins by about 5 basis points," Xing said.
"The aim is to stabilise profitability in the financial sector and strengthen its capacity to absorb risks," he added, noting the measure is unlikely to have a material impact on the stock market.

Separately, Chinese regulators, including the central bank, will hold meetings with financial institutions on Monday to discuss tools to support capital markets, media reported, as turbulence in stocks and bonds fuels calls for policy support.

The PBOC said last month that it was considering making the overnight reverse repurchase rate its main policy rate, in an effort to improve the transmission of monetary policy and support economic growth.
1de26d12e871a363: ALOR SETAR, Nov 2 — The issue of sedimentation along the ferry lane in the waters of Kuala Kedah requires a more sustainable, long-term solution to ensure the smooth operation of ferry services to Langkawi.
Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook said dredging works are carried out periodically every two years to prevent sedimentation from disrupting operations in the area.
However, he noted that a more comprehensive solution must be sought, given that this issue continues to be an operational constraint at the terminal.

“There are physical constraints because the passenger terminal currently under development is situated at its original location. Reclaiming land from the sea or developing new areas would be prohibitively expensive.
“Therefore, we are seeking a long-term solution to address this sedimentation issue, while dredging works are being carried out periodically,” he said.
He told reporters after officiating a ceremony to distribute special financial aid to taxi, rental car, and school bus drivers in the state of Kedah here today.
Meanwhile, Loke encouraged both existing and new ferry operators to expand their services and increase trip frequencies to better meet the needs of users.

However, he noted that any increase in the number of trips would depend on the operators’ capabilities, taking into account various factors such as operating costs, passenger volume, and operational constraints.

7fb9a7867b9980e7: KUALA LUMPUR: Bowling will offer 22 gold medals at the 2027 SEA Games, giving hosts Malaysia a platform to test an expanded format designed to revive the sport's international profile.
The programme doubles the 11 events contested when Malaysia last hosted the Games in 2017, introducing separate titles across short, medium and long oil patterns.
For Malaysian Tenpin Bowling Congress (MTBC) secretary-general Maradona Chok, the initiative extends beyond securing medals for the host nation.
"We want to shake the bowling world, not just Malaysia, but open the eyes of bowlers around the world to such a possibility," Maradona said.
"We want the message to go out about what it could mean for bowling."
The drive comes as bowling struggles for relevance on multi-sport stages. Olympic inclusion remains elusive, while the sport last featured at the Asian Games in Indonesia in 2018.
It was omitted from the Hangzhou edition in 2023, the 2026 Aichi-Nagoya Games, and the 2023 SEA Games in Cambodia.
The final list, approved by the SEA Games Federation executive committee on Oct 30, allocates eight men's, eight women's, and six mixed events to bowling.
Men's and women's singles and doubles will each award short, medium and long-pattern gold medals.
Mixed doubles and mixed teams of four will adopt the same format.
Men's and women's trios and teams of five, contested as three-block events, complete the programme.
The masters event has been excluded.
Oil patterns determine ball reaction, equipment choices, and delivery angles.
Organisers believe pattern-specific titles will allow specialists to flourish, though competition rules will dictate squad deployment.
Maradona said the Asian Bowling Federation and International Bowling Federation have formally endorsed the trial.
"Both gave me a letter to MASOC saying they were excited about testing the format at the SEA Games and were supportive of it."
Maradona added that he hopes the format eventually gains traction at the Asian Games.
While Malaysia remain a regional heavyweight, the expanded programme will also benefit regional rivals.
Traditional contenders Singapore, Indonesia, Thailand, and the Philippines are expected to field strong squads, alongside emerging nations such as Vietnam.
The expansion places bowling joint fifth alongside silat by medal count, behind aquatics, athletics, cycling, and gymnastics.
Its 22 gold medals represent nearly 5 per cent of the 473 events across 43 sports.
The elevated platform is expected to strengthen national associations' lobbying efforts for state funding and athlete development.
However, medal proliferation alone will not guarantee bowling's return to larger multi-sport games.
Malaysia's test will be to deliver an interesting competition and establish a format other international organisers wish to adopt.

df94f658fc438447: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit may weaken against the US dollar next year but could still outperform several major Asian currencies, according to HSBC.
The bank said resilient domestic fundamentals will help the ringgit cushion pressure from a stronger greenback and widening interest rate differentials.
HSBC expects the ringgit to trade between RM4.10 and RM4.20 against the US dollar in 2027, compared with its current range of RM4.05-RM4.10.
HSBC Asia FX Research head Joey Chew said the local currency will remain under pressure from sustained US dollar strength, interest rate differentials and potential political uncertainties.

Chew expects the ringgit to fare better than the Thai baht, Indonesian rupiah and Philippine peso, as those economies face greater exposure to higher oil import costs, relatively low interest rates and domestic political or policy uncertainties.

The ringgit may, however, underperform some North Asian currencies, particularly the yuan and South Korean won, which are benefiting from stronger semiconductor export revenues and efforts to promote greater international use of their currencies.
She said the ringgit had largely traded between RM4.05 and RM4.10 since the second quarter, after briefly strengthening beyond RM4 in the first quarter.
"After the midterms, there's a bit of volatility in the dollar, but the US Fed is expected to hike in December, so we can get that little bit of dollar strength at the end of the year," she said.
Speaking at HSBC's foreign exchange investment outlook today, Chew said the ringgit's trading range could shift higher next year as the US dollar maintained its strength.
"Into next year, our view for now is still that we have a bit of a range, but the range might shift a little bit higher," she said.
"So instead of RM4.05 to RM4.10, we might go into a RM4.10 to RM4.20 range."
She said Malaysia's political calendar could also influence investor sentiment, as global investors might become more cautious towards markets facing potential political changes.

The US midterm elections could also affect the ringgit indirectly through their implications for global technology investments, particularly if investors reassessed the artificial intelligence (AI) investment outlook.

Chew said investor positioning remained heavily concentrated in US technology stocks, particularly AI-related companies, leaving markets vulnerable to a significant correction if confidence in the sector weakened.
The impact on Malaysia would depend on whether any correction remained confined to company valuations or spilled over into investment spending and regional supply chains.

"If it spills over into what exports in Asia, including Malaysia, are doing, because of what it means for AI capital expenditure, capital expansion, investments, all these data centre investments in Malaysia and the region," she said.
"All these exports that Malaysian companies are doing for the data centres, if it affects that outlook, then actually ringgit will also be affected negatively next year," she added.
Ringgit Caught Between Dollar, Yuan
Chew said the ringgit was being pulled in opposing directions by a strengthening US dollar and the persistent appreciation of the Chinese yuan.
The dollar's rebound had prevented the ringgit from strengthening beyond RM4, while the yuan's gains had limited further weakness in the local currency.
"The dollar-ringgit is sort of stuck between these two. On the one hand, it cannot drop below four.
"On the other hand, because of the dollar-Chinese yuan, because of renminbi strength, it also doesn't have enough momentum to weaken much more than, say, four ten," she said.
She said the relationship between the ringgit and yuan remained significant given Malaysia's open economy and close economic exposure to both the US and China.
Rate Gap Clouds Bond Inflows
Interest rate differentials between Malaysia and the US are another source of pressure on the ringgit, particularly as markets anticipate further monetary tightening by the Federal Reserve (Fed).

Chew said HSBC expected the Fed to raise interest rates another one or two times, while markets were also anticipating an increase in Malaysia's overnight policy rate (OPR), although the expected magnitude was considerably smaller.
A wider negative interest rate differential could encourage Malaysian residents to seek higher returns overseas, including through investments in higher-yielding bonds and other foreign assets.
Chew noted that resident investment outflows in Malaysia reached a record high in the second quarter.
Meanwhile, foreign bond inflows might not provide equivalent support for the ringgit, as some investors could hedge their currency exposure while capturing higher yields.

"On the foreigners' side, there are some inflows. A lot of the bond inflows are positive. However, the interest rate differential makes it worthwhile for foreigners to buy Malaysian bonds on an FX hedge basis," she said.

"They actually get the yield pickup when they buy MGS and FX hedge at the same time. So some of these bond inflows that we see may not necessarily help this currency because they might be FX hedged," she added.
Separately, HSBC economists expect Bank Negara Malaysia to raise the OPR in the first quarter of 2027.
Chew said persistent inflationary pressures from elevated oil prices and the potential impact of El Nino on prices across Asia would leave central banks with limited room for monetary easing.

"As long as oil prices, as long as inflation, as long as this idea of this El Nino affecting inflation in Asia remains, I don't think any central bank, including Malaysia, despite having such controlled inflation rates, is able to have this luxury of thinking about rate cuts," she said.

e0c677ff34a8c734: KUALA LUMPUR: The High Court was told today that the family of political aide Teoh Beng Hock had no excuse for its delay in bringing judicial review proceedings against the police, having known for more than seven years that no murder investigation was opened into his death.

Senior federal counsel Sallehuddin Ali, appearing for the police, said the case was reclassified in 2019 as involving wrongful confinement under Section 342 of the Penal Code, a year after the Pakatan Harapan administration took power.
He said the family previously voiced concerns over the slow pace of the investigation and asked whether the probe papers had been referred to the Attorney-General's Chambers.
"Despite having that knowledge, they only filed their application for judicial review after the statutory three-month deadline lapsed.

"They claim that, to date, no Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission officer has been charged over the deceased's death, and that they would be denied justice if their judicial review application is not heard," he said in opposing the family's application for an extension of time.
The Teoh family is seeking to compel the police to open a murder investigation into his death 17 years ago.
The family members claim they only discovered in a letter received from the police in January this year that no investigations for murder or culpable homicide not amounting to murder were initiated.

Lawyer Lim Wei Jiet, who appeared for the family, said they previously wrote to both the police and the attorney-general seeking clarification on whether investigations had ever been carried out under Sections 302 (murder) or 304 (causing death) of the Penal Code, but received no response.
"Yet the government comes before the court today and says our application was filed out of time.

"Even it the court is not with us on the merits, we urge it to grant an extension of time because this case has been a matter of significant public interest for many years and the family remains in the dark about what happened to him," he said.
Justice Norliza Othman fixed Nov 17 to decide whether to grant the family’s application for an extension of time.

Teoh, an aide to then Selangor executive councillor Ean Yong Hian Wah, was found dead in July 2009 on the fifth floor of Plaza Masalam in Shah Alam, hours after he arrived for questioning at the Selangor MACC office.
An inquest initially returned an open verdict. However, in 2014, the Court of Appeal ruled that his death was caused by "one or more unknown persons", including MACC officers.
Two special investigation teams were set up in 2011 and 2015 to probe Teoh’s death, but both probes were classified as NFA or no further action by the public prosecutor.
Police completed the probe on wrongful confinement last year, following a court order in 2024, but the AGC directed that the case be classified as NFA.
The AGC said there was insufficient proof to establish an offence against any individual under the law.

5e86ff59f937d1c9: KUALA LUMPUR: Travel technology provider Amadeus IT Group says it has taken measures to fix a security vulnerability that made certain booking information accessible, following reports of customer data exposure involving several international airlines.
The Spain-based company said its investigations are continuing but there is no evidence that payment or financial information had been accessed.
"Certain booking-display data was accessible through the vulnerability. Although our investigations continue, we can confirm that there is no evidence that payment or financial data was accessed."
"There are no indications that this vulnerability has been exploited for ransomware purposes," Amadeus said in a statement shared to Business Times.
The company said it has implemented measures to address the vulnerability and strengthened its monitoring and detection capabilities.
It added that it is in direct communication with its customers and relevant authorities.
Several airlines recently announced that their passenger reservation data held by their third-party technology provider, Amadeus, were breached.
On Oct 31, Malaysia Airlines Bhd said certain customer information processed through Amadeus between August 2023 and September 2026 may have been affected by the cybersecurity incident.
However, the national carrier's own IT systems had not been compromised and there was currently no evidence that financial information had been accessed.
Malaysia Airlines said it was working closely with Amadeus and relevant parties to investigate the incident and assess its impact.
On Oct 30, Cathay Pacific said about 53,000 bookings were affected by unauthorised access to passenger reservation data held by Amadeus.
The Hong Kong-based airline said most affected records included booking references, passenger names and flight details.
A smaller number of records may also have included email addresses, phone numbers, travel document information and frequent flyer numbers.
Cathay Pacific said there was no evidence that financial or payment information had been accessed, while its own systems and operations remained unaffected.
The airline said it was notified by Amadeus on Oct 28 and received further details the following day.
Cathay Pacific said the unauthorised access involved login credentials assigned to an Amadeus system account, with affected reservation records dating between August 2023 and September 2026.
Other airlines affected by the incident include Japan Airlines and Japan Transocean Air, which reported that about 92,000 customers were affected.
All Nippon Airways said information relating to about 37,800 customers had also been accessed.
South Korea's Korean Air and Asiana Airlines have also reported unauthorised access to customer reservation information through Amadeus but have not disclosed the number of affected customers.
Korean Air and Asiana Airlines were notified of the incident on Oct 20, while Japan Airlines and Japan Transocean Air received notification on Oct 23.
Several affected airlines have advised customers to remain vigilant against suspicious emails, fraudulent phone calls and other communications requesting personal or financial information.

On Sept 5, the four disputed Negeri Sembilan undangs claimed that Ismail signed the proclamation seeking to remove Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir as Yang Dipertuan Besar.
The menteri besar initially sidestepped the allegation and declared full loyalty to the ruler, prompting the undangs to produce the purported proclamation signed by Ismail at a press conference.
Ismail then claimed that he signed the document "unwillingly and under coercion", and maintained that the proclamation was invalid. He also lodged a police report on Sept 8.
However, he later endorsed a state executive council statement announcing Tuanku Muhriz’s purported removal as ruler.
Two weeks ago, home minister Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the probe paper was still with the AGC.

7394cce9a73ed861: HANG TUAH JAYA: Calon Pakatan Harapan (PH) DUN Kuala Linggi, Muhammad Mukhlisul Mubin Julasapiyah, berazam bekerja lebih keras untuk memenangi hati pengundi, mengambil inspirasi daripada perjuangan bapanya yang lima kali kalah di kerusi itu.

Beliau yang lebih dikenali dengan panggilan Mukhlis berkata, mahu membawa pendekatan politik baharu dan segar di Kuala Linggi, selain mengembalikan keyakinan golongan muda terhadap peranan ahli politik dalam meningkatkan kualiti hidup masyarakat.

Mengulas kritikan di media sosial, termasuk dakwaan berkaitan kelayakan akademiknya, Mukhlis berkata beliau tidak menganggapnya sebagai pembulian kerana kecaman dan tekanan adalah risiko yang perlu diterima apabila menceburi politik.

Dalam pada itu, Mukhlis menafikan dakwaan beliau gagal menamatkan pengajian ijazah sarjana muda undang-undang di Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia (UKM).

Mukhlis, calon termuda pada PRN kali ini, membuat penampilan sulung dalam pilihan raya bakal berdepan saingan tiga penjuru menentang penyandang daripada Barisan Nasional, Rosli Abdullah, serta Farhana Hamzah daripada Parti Bersama Malaysia (Bersama).

5bc960c6944e4340: SAGADA: Tiny pinewood bonfires burned through the night at a mountain cemetery as the largely Christian Philippines remembered its dead, turning the fog-shrouded hilltop into a vast, fragrant altar of light.

The eerie Panag-aapoy ("to light a fire") ceremony in the tourist town of Sagada has marked All Saints' Day for the past 122 years, said Winston Garlejo Menong, director of the Episcopal Church of Saint Mary the Virgin, which owns the cemetery.
As night crept in and darkness blanketed the four-hectare burial ground, the hum of activity and thick smoke gave way to a sepulchral glow as fires burned for its more than 2,000 dead.

The Cordillera mountain region's animist residents adopted Christianity only after Spain ceded the Philippines to the United States in 1898, four centuries after Spanish friars had converted the people of the coasts to Catholicism.
US Protestant missionaries encouraged Sagada's residents to bury their dead and light candles on their graves, he said.
"In our Biblical context, Christ is the light," Menong said.
Be it with candles or the pine sticks preferred in Sagada, lighting a flame is "inviting the presence of Christ with us, having fellowship with our departed loved ones", he said.

Sagada's first Christians burned pinewood because candles were expensive and their flames were easily snuffed out by wind – unlike the brisk burn of the aromatic, sap-rich pines that cover the Cordilleras, Sagada tourism officer Maria Teresa Abad told AFP.
The practice echoes the burning of incense in Buddhist rituals, though pine's sharp natural scent makes it stand out from the aromatic powders used in joss sticks.
Cybil Domoguen returned to Sagada this year with her father and a bundle of 20-inch (51 centimetre) pine sticks to honour the grandparents who had raised her there.
"It's very unusual that people actually come here to watch. Usually one comes to the cemetery to pray for a dead relative," the 31-year-old teacher told AFP.
"If a grave does not have any visitors, people make sure to light some sticks for them."
Like others participating in the ceremony, she has conflicted feelings about the growing tourist presence.
"Last year, there were tourists who were taking pictures of us, which was uncomfortable," she added.
"We have no problem with strangers as long as they respect boundaries."
The people of Sagada did not always light flames over their dead, or even bury them.

Before the missionaries arrived, the preferred practice was to hang coffins from the walls of cliffs or wedge them into the mouths of caves, a custom that only fully died out in 2010, Abad, the tourism officer, said.
Some of the "hanging coffins" can still be seen on nearby Sagada cliffs.
"Traditional burial beliefs associate caves and elevated burial places with the spirit's passage toward the ancestral realm", something burial would hinder, she said.
It also had the practical benefit of keeping remains safe from wild animals and flooding.

Over time, as Sagada's mild climate and abundant waterfalls turned it into a popular refuge from the tropical heat, the Panag-aapoy – and the hanging coffins – became massive tourist draws in themselves, to the chagrin of residents.
The church and local government have since taken steps to protect the region's cultural heritage.
Picnic mats and drone photography were banned, and noisy, mobile-phone-toting tourists were kept well away from the graves and cautioned to observe respectful silence.
"Panag-aapoy is a sacred cultural tradition, NOT a festival or a tourism event," the Philippine tourism ministry said in a seasonal advisory.
"The solemnity of the practice was getting lost," Menong said with a sigh. "It was turning into a muppet show."
Rex Refuela, a 46-year-old tourist from Manila attending his first Panag-aapoy, told AFP he understood the need to be respectful.
"It's OK to have some restrictions to keep and maintain its solemnity," he said.
"It's so amazingly beautiful."

cd11e3468a5b7f7f: GEORGE TOWN: Former chief minister Lim Guan Eng wants the state government to establish a State Commission of Inquiry (SCI) into the fatal landslide in Taman Seri Rambai, Paya Terubong.
His call follows a similar appeal by a coalition of Penang non-governmental organisations (NGOs) last week.

Debating the state's 2027 Budget at the state legislative assembly, the Air Putih assemblyman said an independent and impartial investigation was essential to ensure all responsible parties were held accountable.
The landslide occurred behind a residence along Lebuh Rambai 13 in Taman Seri Rambai on the morning of Oct 25.
It claimed the life of 73-year-old medical practitioner Dr Wong Kar Lin and forced the evacuation of six neighbouring homes.
"To honour Dr Wong's memory and ensure justice for her family, the government must ensure those responsible are held fully accountable.
"An SCI is needed to ensure that not only the developer and landowner, but all other relevant parties, bear appropriate responsibility," Lim said.
Lim also denied online allegations that he had approved the project during his tenure as chief minister from 2008 to 2018.

Clarifying the timeline, Lim said site signboards showed that planning permission was only approved in 2023. Earthwork and building plans were approved in 2024 under the current developer, Sunrich Conquest Sdn Bhd.
"In 2023 and 2024, I was neither chief minister nor finance minister," he said.
He added that he had instructed his legal team to take action against those spreading the defamatory allegations.
The Penang government has held the developer and landowner of the condominium and road project responsible for the fatal landslide.
Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow has warned of possible legal consequences, saying the landslide occurred on the developer's land.
He said the parties were responsible for ensuring site safety and implementing mitigation measures.
On other governance issues, Lim wants the state government to table the RM24.6 billion Perak-Penang Bulk Water Supply Agreement at the assembly for open debate.
He said non-disclosure agreements must not keep taxpayers in the dark about a 40-year deal that runs until 2072.

He also questioned why the state government had not revoked the contract for the RM1 billion project involving the reclamation of 70 acres at Karpal Singh Drive and the rehabilitation of the 84-acre Jelutong landfill.
This followed reports that the Department of Environment had rejected the contractor's applications five times.
Lim also proposed that the state establish a traditional Special Financial Zone (SFZ) spanning 40 hectares in Ampang Jajar, Seberang Prai.
He said the proposed zone would complement the RM100 million federally funded Penang Technology Financial Centre and help balance economic development on the mainland.

7a147f5b767db40b: KUALA LUMPUR: National men's doubles coach Herry Iman Piengardi has urged fans to temper expectations and avoid making premature comparisons involving rising pair Aaron Tai-Yap Roy King.

The young duo have drawn comparisons to South Korea's world No. 1 Kim Won Ho-Seo Seung Jae, while Aaron's left-handed, attacking style has prompted fans to liken him to former Olympic silver medallist Yap Kim Hock.
However, Herry said Aaron and Kim Hock play differently despite their similar physical build.
Roy King, 25, is Kim Hock's nephew.
Kim Hock partnered Cheah Soon Kit to win men's doubles silver medals at the 1996 Atlanta Olympics and 1997 Glasgow World Championships.
"They have just started as a pair and have a long way to go. I hope the fans can be patient and not jump into any comparisons. Aaron-Roy King are creating their own style of play," Herry said.
"They still have their shortcomings, and we have to give them time to mature into a strong pair. They are still untested and haven't faced all the top pairs.
"All I can say is they have a good future. Let them grow."
Aaron, 20, and Roy King made an impact at the Arctic Open in Vantaa, Finland, last month, winning the Super 500 title.
Subsequent losses to world No. 4 compatriots Aaron Chia and Soh Wooi Yik at the Denmark Open, and Won Ho and Seung Jae at the French Open, checked their momentum.

However, they recovered at the Hylo Open last week, defeating Indonesia's world No. 7 Sabar Karyaman-Moh Reza Isfahani, as well as Taiwan's 15th-ranked pair Chiu Hsiang Chieh-Wang Chi Lin, to reach the semi-finals.
They were eventually stopped by Denmark's world No. 26 Christian Faust Kjaer and Rasmus Kjaer, who went on to take the title.
Aaron-Roy King will skip this week's Korea Open and return to tournament action at the Kumamoto Masters from Nov 10-15, followed by the Hong Kong Open from Nov 17-22.
7c2633aa1d3ec7fd: GEORGE TOWN: Former chief minister Lim Guan Eng has questioned the six-month bonus paid to Penang Development Corporation (PDC) staff despite what he described as serious project mismanagement.
Debating the state's 2027 Budget at the state legislative assembly, the Air Putih assemblyman cited findings from the Auditor-General's Report 2026.
The report revealed that PDC's road and bridge upgrading project from Jalan Perusahaan to Jalan Tok Kangar was delayed by 2,278 days and incurred a 47 per cent cost overrun.
"The project cost ballooned from an initial RM43 million to RM63.4 million, an increase of RM20.4 million.
"Despite the Auditor-General's reprimand, a six-month bonus was still paid to PDC staff for 2024. The payment was disbursed in February 2025," he said.

It was reported in February 2025 that 396 PDC employees would receive bonuses ranging from one to six months' salary. It was the highest payout in the corporation's history since its establishment in 1969.
Its chief executive officer Datuk Aziz Bakar said the bonuses were awarded following the corporation's record profit of more than RM500 million in 2024.
Lim wants the state government to hold PDC officers accountable for the project's inefficiencies.
These included a RM3.12 million progress payment made to a finishing contractor before a formal contract had been signed.
He said the corporation's poor track record raised doubts about its ability to develop the 1,142-acre Batu Kawan Industrial Park 2 (BKIP2) project on its own.
Lim also recalled the controversy surrounding the direct sale of 559 acres of PDC-owned land in Byram Estate, within BKIP2.
The land was initially sold for RM646 million without an open tender.
He said that when a subsequent open request for proposal (RFP) was called, the purchase price rose to RM818 million, which was RM172 million higher than the original direct-deal price.
"With such a track record, will BKIP2 face the same fate of a seven-year delay and a 40 per cent cost overrun?
"A new open-tender RFP or a joint venture with the private sector may be safer, more financially rewarding and allow for quicker development," he added.
The issue led to a clash between Lim and current Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow in May this year.
Chow and PDC defended the decision to reject the Aspen-linked consortium's bid, saying it had failed to meet five of the nine key RFP conditions.
f7ae0e8b2f3e942f: KUALA LUMPUR: Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman (Muda-Muar) mempertahankan perjanjian keyakinan dan perbekalan (CSA) yang ditandatanganinya dengan kerajaan minggu lalu atas alasan ia menyediakan ruang yang mendorong dua reformasi institusi penting.
Menurutnya, perjanjian itu penting bukan hanya untuk memastikan peruntukan kawasan yang adil dan saksama kepada Ahli Parlimen, tetapi turut mengurangkan pemusatan kuasa di tangan perdana menteri.
Di bawah CSA, kerajaan berjanji mengehadkan tempoh jawatan perdana menteri serta memisahkan peranan peguam negara (AG) dan pendakwa raya sebelum tamat penggal pentadbirannya.
Syed Saddiq berkata, pemisahan peranan peguam negara dan pendakwa raya akan menghalang perdana menteri serta Jemaah Menteri daripada mengawal pelantikan bagi jawatan tertinggi dalam badan pendakwaan.

"Ini akan mengurangkan kemungkinan kes rasuah membabitkan sekutu politik digugurkan atau Jabatan Peguam Negara (AGC) mahupun Suruhanjaya Pencegahan Rasuah Malaysia (SPRM) disalah guna sebagai senjata terhadap lawan politik," katanya ketika membahas Belanjawan 2027 di peringkat jawatankuasa.
Beliau berkata, semua pihak, sama ada sekutu atau seteru politik, perlu diadili di mahkamah berdasarkan fakta dan bukti kes, bukannya dipengaruhi kuasa perdana menteri.
Bekas presiden Muda itu memeterai CSA dengan Putrajaya minggu lalu bersama enam Ahli Parlimen Bersatu yang diketuai Presidennya, Muhyiddin Yassin.
Ahli Parlimen Perikatan Nasional mengkritik perjanjian itu dengan mendakwa ia akan menghalang tujuh Ahli Parlimen pembangkang terbabit daripada memainkan peranan semak dan imbang terhadap kerajaan.
Syed Saddiq berkata, beliau turut menyokong CSA yang dimeterainya dengan kerajaan pimpinan Ismail Sabri Yaakob dan Pakatan Harapan pada September 2021.

Menurutnya, reformasi yang dicadangkan di bawah CSA perlu merangkumi penggubalan undang-undang bagi memastikan peruntukan sama rata disalurkan kepada semua Ahli Parlimen sebelum tamat penggal Parlimen.
Jika tidak, katanya, kitaran tindak balas politik akan berulang, dengan Ahli Parlimen pembangkang terus dinafikan peruntukan pembangunan kawasan oleh kerajaan.
b14b1ac9b8a704d5: MELAKA: Melaka aims to have 300 electric vehicle (EV) charging units by 2027 as it steps up efforts to strengthen infrastructure to support the growing automotive industry.

0df49bfbc0bb7e09: SINGAPORE, Nov 2 — What started as a fundraising appeal for the orphaned son of the couple killed in the Tampines Ave 12 crash, soon found itself under scrutiny after online users questioned the legitimacy of the drive.
The allegations prompted its organiser to publicly defend the appeal.
As of today, donations for the fundraiser had exceeded S$428,000 (RM1.4 million).
The fundraiser was started by a relative of one of the deceased victims following the fatal Tampines crash.
The Tampines Ave 12 multi-vehicle accident on Thursday (October 29) killed the 24-year-old rider and his wife, who was also 24. The couple were reportedly expecting their second child.
News of the plight of their first child, now orphaned, spread online, with many netizens asking how they could contribute to or donate to the grieving family.
Online user "sgfirecouple" shared how the fundraising organiser had originally responded to his story, saying she was heartened by the amount of support the family was receiving online.
The organiser subsequently shared an Instagram story (IGS) of herself and a boy, allegedly the deceased couple's son, along with a Paynow QR code, inviting interested netizens to make a contribution.
She also said that while donations were being sent to her personal bank account, she was working with the family to open a bank account for the couple's son.
Donations vs doubt
Questions over the fundraiser's legitimacy surfaced over the weekend when a Facebook user claimed she did not know who the fundraising organiser was.
Her caption read, "Stop sharing the donation and do not scan the PayNow. We don't know this person."
Around the same time, the fundraising organiser created a Give.Asia fundraising page and began sharing it, along with a picture of the deceased couple and their son.
In her new post, she said that she had to censor the little boy's face due to a gag order.
The fundraising organiser subsequently addressed the concerns in a series of Instagram Stories.
According to her, the original PayNow QR code was shared after family members, friends and followers asked how they could contribute.
As interest in the case grew, she decided to move the fundraising effort to Give.Asia.

The organiser, via her IGS, said that all donations which had originally come through via the Paynow were properly recorded "to ensure complete transparency", and that the Paynow QR code has since expired.
She added that the funds received would be used solely for the child's education, medical expenses and other needs.
According to the organiser, she has also clarified any misunderstandings regarding the fundraising with relevant parties.
Setting up fundraisers in Singapore

In her IGS, the organiser said that setting up a fundraiser in Singapore was not easy and that there were documentation steps and verification steps involved, attempting to further-prove her legitimacy.
Since social issues began garnering attention online, more Singaporeans have been turning to virtual fundraising platforms to set up fundraisers.

However, when setting up a fundraiser, the organiser is usually required to submit documentation before a campaign is approved - documentation can be in the form of a hospital letter, hospital bills, invoices or legal letters.
Platforms like give.asia require fundraisers to submit all relevant documentation before granting approval for the fundraiser to be published.
Other platforms such as giving.sg conduct relevant checks before approving a campaign to be published on their site.
The fundraiser involving the Tampines fatal crash, "Help an orphan: A community coming together for his future", has since received over S$428,000 in donations from more than 11,000 donors. — AsiaOne
e44a9dff6ac655fe: KUALA LUMPUR: Sepang International Circuit (SIC) expects the Formula One feasibility study to be presented to cabinet by the end of this month.
SIC chief executive officer Azhan Shafriman Hanif said it is then entirely up to the government to decide whether or not to bring F1 back to Malaysia on a permanent basis.
"We expect it to happen at the end of November, or possibly in the third week," he said yesterday.
"Available F1 slots will be discussed at the cabinet level. We will leave it to the government to decide.
"The slots which are open to us only begin in 2029. But we will also discuss other things which we can do in the near term with F1."
Shafriman stressed that bringing F1 back to Sepang will be a massive undertaking that requires a whole-of-government approach.
"F1 is not something that you decide today and do tomorrow, it is not like that," he said.

"It is a national project. I would say that the approach taken by the Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim is the right one, we need a whole-of-government approach and work together with all ministries as well as the private sector."
The Malaysian Grand Prix F1 race was held at Sepang from 1999 to 2017 before it was dropped by the government due to escalating hosting costs and the sport's dwindling popularity.
Sepang, however, acted as a replacement venue for the Bahrain GP last month due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. Bahrain footed the majority of the expenses.
Despite teething transport issues on the first few days, the event was seen as a huge success which drew a record attendance of 261,000 fans across the three-day event.
Bringing F1 back to Malaysia on a permanent basis, however, will not be cheap.
It is expected to cost Malaysia at least RM300 million to organise - the bulk of which is rights fees paid to F1 - for each edition.
2ef653dfe9c3f8bc: PETALING JAYA: Malaysia Aviation Group (MAG) has obtained the highest possible rating for its Islamic sukuk programme from MARC Ratings, in the agency's inaugural credit rating of the aviation firm.
In a press release, MAG said this reflected the group's steady financial discipline, operational performance and ongoing execution of the third iteration of its long-term business plan.

MAG also said it is actively advancing key strategic projects to support the momentum of its next phase of transformation, as it seeks to build capacity and expedite commercial expansion.
This includes investments to modernise its fleet, grow its network and expand infrastructure, including the development of a new in-flight catering facility.
MAG said it continuously evaluates diverse, proactive capital options that align with its financial goals, such as the sukuk programme, to fund its initiatives sustainably.

MAG president and group CEO Nasaruddin A Bakar said the company's trajectory under its long-term business plan was guided by sound financial planning, operational rigour and clear commercial priorities.

"MARC Ratings’s affirmation provides support for our strategic direction as we plan beyond 2030. We remain focused on pursuing growth in a measured way, including enhancing our network and in-flight services and scaling our technical maintenance, repair and overhaul capabilities.
"These investments also contribute to Malaysia's ambition to become a leading regional aerospace hub, and support the development of the national aviation ecosystem," Nasaruddin said.
ffdbf05d871bd33e: BENGALURU: Carlos Alcaraz expects the battle at the top of men's tennis to be more than a two-horse race with Jannik Sinner in 2027 after Alexander Zverev broke their stranglehold on the Grand Slams and Ben Shelton showed signs he could become part of the elite.
Alcaraz split the four Grand Slams with Sinner in the 2024 and 2025 seasons, but injuries to the top two this year left the door open, with Zverev winning the French Open and US Open.
With Shelton reaching the Flushing Meadows final, Alcaraz expected no shortage of genuine contenders for the big titles.
"Pre-season is really important," Alcaraz told reporters after his Vienna Open triumph on Sunday.
"I can tell you that players are taking pre-season really seriously, those weeks of training hard to be in good shape.

"Sascha (Zverev) showed us what he's capable of doing. The best player of this year. He deserves to be there. Let's see if he's going to continue to do the great things he's been doing this year in 2027.

"Shelton reached his first Grand Slam final and I think he's ambitious and hungry for more next year. A couple of others also playing great and they're going to try to practice at their best to be at their best next year.
"I don't like to say it's going to be Jannik and me and the rest. Let's see who's going to be there. I'm pretty sure that a lot of players are going to show up."
Alcaraz won his seventh Grand Slam title at the Australian Open before a wrist injury kept him out for more than four months. Since returning at the US Open, he has won titles in Tokyo and Vienna.
He will look to finish the season on a high at this week's Paris Masters and the ATP Finals from Nov 15.
f9220c6d6f428a3b: NEW DELHI: A second cyclone in less than a week headed for India's eastern coast on Monday, with the storm expected to hit overnight, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said.
Cyclone Murasu is expected to make landfall around midnight on Monday or in the early hours of Tuesday, bringing heavy rain to Andhra Pradesh and neighbouring Tamil Nadu.
The storm season has been intensified by the El Nino weather phenomenon, which has contributed to unprecedented warming, bringing worldwide changes in winds, pressure and rainfall patterns.
"It is very likely to... cross south Andhra Pradesh coast as a severe cyclonic storm with wind speeds of around 100 to 110 kilometres per hour, gusting 120 kmph," IMD said.
The storm is expected to make landfall between Nellore and Narsapur, near the city of Ongole, it said.
Last Wednesday, Cyclone Arnab struck the Andhra Pradesh coast, bringing heavy rain and killing at least three people.
Murasu is expected to be weaker in terms of wind speed than its predecessor, but could bring further heavy rain to areas already affected.
Cyclones, called hurricanes in the North Atlantic and typhoons in the Pacific, are a regular menace in the Bay of Bengal and northern Indian Ocean.
The weather office warned that strong winds could damage thatched houses, tear off rooftops and uproot trees, while standing crops, plantations and orchards could also suffer damage.
8e1f4ce12f4c6801: SINGAPORE, Nov 2 — A man charged with murdering an elderly man at the void deck of a Telok Blangah HDB block was taken back to the alleged crime scene this morning.

Officers responding to the incident then found a 73-year-old Chinese man lying motionless on the ground floor, while a 53-year-old Chinese man was also found injured.

Foong arrived back at the block at about 9.15am and was escorted by six police investigators.
Dressed in a red polo shirt and navy blue shorts, he was restrained at his wrists and ankles as he recounted the events of that day.

65bffb0f65e3c6bc: KUALA LUMPUR: A good idea can start anywhere - including in the mind of a child wondering how something around them could be done better.

That is the thinking behind Goodday KidSTART 4.0, which returns for a fourth season with an expanded programme aimed at helping young Malaysians develop creativity, confidence and practical problem-solving skills.
Recognised by the Malaysia Book of Records as the country’s largest kidpreneur programme, KidSTART began with 340 participants in its first year and reached 8,000 students by Season 3.

This year, the programme will take participants through school roadshows, workshops, bootcamps and mentorship before culminating in a national finale. For the first time, the journey will also extend to the big screen through a film inspired by the programme and its young participants.

Backed by the education ministry, KidSTART is designed to complement classroom learning by introducing children to entrepreneurship in practical ways. Participants are encouraged to identify real-world problems, develop possible solutions and turn their ideas into workable concepts, while selected students will receive further guidance as they progress through the competition.
Amy Gan, vice-president of marketing at Etika Sdn Bhd and spokesperson for Goodday Milk, said the aim was to give children more opportunities to develop their ideas beyond the competition itself.
“Instead of their journey ending with the competition, we want to create something that can continue to be seen, shared and talked about beyond the season,” she said.
Gan added that the programme was also intended to nurture curiosity, creativity and confidence through practical experiences and exposure.

Entries are now open to children across Malaysia. To take part, participants must submit a one-minute video introducing themselves and presenting a business idea through the official Goodday KidSTART website.
The top 300 entrants will advance to an online workshop and bootcamp, where they will receive coaching and mentorship to further develop their ideas and sharpen their pitches.

Shortlisted participants will then move through an intensive bootcamp before the finalists take to the stage at the Grand Finale. There, they will present their ideas to a panel of judges and a live audience, with winners receiving a share of RM60,000 worth of prizes to help develop their ideas further.
Gan said the decision to take KidSTART beyond television and onto the big screen was intended to give the children’s ideas a wider audience, including parents and families.
Submissions are now open at the official Goodday KidSTART website.
27e7c0b7331e2fbd: PETALING JAYA: Police are investigating three lawyers representing the family of Noorizwan Zulkefly, who died in custody last month, for allegedly harassing a forensic specialist.
Bukit Aman criminal investigation department director M Kumar said the doctor in question, a civil servant, lodged a report against the lawyers, Bernama reported.

The case is being investigated for criminal intimidation, obstructing a public servant from discharging their duties, and threat of injury to a public servant under Sections 506, 186 and 189 of the Penal Code.
"The doctor is a civil servant and a police report has been lodged by her. An investigation is ongoing," he said.
Kumar said police had recorded statements from the doctor and the three lawyers, while statements from Noorizwan’s family members were being taken.

Noorizwan, 42, was arrested on Sept 20 and held at the Cheras police headquarters for 11 days without his family’s knowledge before being taken to Hospital Canselor Tuanku Muhriz UKM on Sept 30. He was pronounced dead on Oct 1.

Lawyers Latheefa Koya, N Surendran and Dina Zamri were questioned by police over a visit to Hospital Canselor Tunku Muhriz UKM’s pathology unit to seek clarification on Noorizwan’s autopsy findings and view photographs of his injuries.
The autopsy reportedly found 21 serious injuries on Noorizwan, including generalised brain haemorrhage, internal abdominal bleeding and extensive swelling from his skull to the soles of his feet.
Kumar said the investigation paper on Noorizwan’s death would be referred to the Attorney-General’s Chambers on Wednesday.
The probe was taken over by Bukit Aman CID's classified crimes unit or D5 and is being conducted under Section 331 of the Penal Code for causing grievous hurt to extort a confession.
Noorizwan's family and lawyers have repeatedly insisted that his death should be probed for murder.
