01ae1eb618827c6d: KUALA LUMPUR: The High Court has dismissed AirAsia's bid to overturn an Industrial Court award of RM268,620 in compensation and back wages to a former pilot who successfully claimed constructive dismissal.
Justice Azizan Arshad upheld the Industrial Court's 2024 decision in favour of Eric Koh, ruling there was no basis for appellate intervention in the case.
"This court finds that the appellant (AirAsia) failed to establish any material error of law or fact in the tribunal's decision.

"The chairman correctly identified the central issue, namely whether the respondent (Koh) was constructively dismissed as a consequence of the company's conduct and whether that conduct amounted to a fundamental breach of the employment contract," he said.
Koh, who started working with the low-cost airline in July 2018, tendered his resignation after he was placed on furlough in 2022 during the Covid-19 pandemic.
The airline reduced Koh’s basic salary by 75% during the period, citing border restrictions which had grounded flights.
Koh claimed he was forced to resign as the decision to slash his pay jeopardised his livelihood.
AirAsia, however, argued that Koh resigned of his own volition.
The Industrial Court ruled that Koh was constructively dismissed and that the low-cost airline had no right to deduct more than 50% of his salary without his consent.
It awarded Koh RM232,320 in back wages and RM36,300 as compensation in lieu of reinstatement.
Lawyers Leow Ho Eng appeared for Koh, while Wendy Lam and Wong Jia Ee represented AirAsia.
AirAsia has appealed this High Court ruling.
fa82b79c48bdbd9a: KUALA LUMPUR: Seorang Ahli Parlimen kerajaan mempersoalkan kelewatan Jabatan Peguam Negara (AGC) memberikan keputusan berhubung kertas siasatan polis berkaitan laporan dibuat Menteri Besar Negeri Sembilan Ismail Lasim.

“Setakat 21 Okt, dimaklumkan polis masih menunggu keputusan dan arahan lanjut daripada Jabatan Peguam Negara berhubung kertas siasatan itu,” kata Cha ketika membahaskan Belanjawan 2027 peringkat jawatankuasa bagi Jabatan Perdana Menteri di Dewan Rakyat.

017d2170d68066d5: SINGAPORE, Nov 2 — It may have seemed like a close shave, but the dramatic landing attempt was all part of standard safety procedures for Singapore Airlines (SIA) pilots.

SIA pilots of flight SQ213 had to approach the runway twice and performed a “go-around” before safely land a plane amid strong winds in Perth, according to a Facebook video by user Chris Perry last Saturday (Oct 31).
The video has garnered over 2.6 million views, 7,300 likes and 1,800 comments as of Monday morning.
In the video, an SIA plane can be seen approaching the runway at Perth Airport.
However, the aircraft is seen abruptly banking to one side, bringing its right wing seemingly close to the ground.
The plane then pulls upward, climbs away from the asphalt and returns to the air before making another landing attempt.
“High winds at Perth caused my sisters flight to have to go round again,” Perry wrote in his post. “Thankfully the second attempt was a success.”
In the comments section, many users pointed out that the wing was quite close to the ground and that the situation looked dangerous.
“Inches away from death, literally,” said one. “That was a very calm and skilled pilot.”
“That wing looks so close to the ground! Far out,” another commented.
Some, however, felt that the video made the incident seem far more dangerous than the situation actually was.
“Pilot checking in. That was pretty sketchy, but not that dangerous,” a user claimed.

“That must have been pretty frightening for many on board. But a go-around is a standard safety procedure and happens regularly at airports around the world,” another stated, adding that SIA only chooses “the best of the best”.
A go-around is a standard procedure in which pilots discontinue an approach or landing and climb away before attempting another landing.
Many users also praised the pilots for their skill in operating the aircraft.
“These pilots are highly trained. They know when to put the kite down or do a go-around for safety.
Another said: “Well done to the pilots, hope your sister wasn’t too shaken up.”
Responding to queries from AsiaOne, an SIA spokesperson said that SQ213 experienced strong winds on approach into Perth International Airport last Saturday.
“As a result, the pilots decided to conduct a go-around,” the spokesperson said. “The Airbus A350-900 aircraft landed safely at 1230hrs (local time) and taxied to the gate.”
SIA also stressed that the safety of customers and crew is their top priority. — AsiaOne
e5c7c1f3c25724e2: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 2 — Government agencies must systematically document their administrative experience and expertise to prevent the loss of institutional knowledge when civil servants retire or are transferred.

Public Service Director-General (KPPA) Tan Sri Dr Wan Ahmad Dahlan Abdul Aziz said knowledge gained through administrative work and research should be preserved and translated into policies, decisions and practical measures.

“Documented experience becomes institutional knowledge that builds the collective memory of the public service,” he said in his keynote address at the opening of the 2026 Research Colloquium at the National Institute of Public Administration (INTAN) here today.
His speech was read by INTAN director Datuk Dr Mohd Zabri Yusoff.
Wan Ahmad Dahlan urged government agencies to document project implementation experiences and administrative challenges through case studies and action research findings.
He also called on department heads and senior management to incorporate research findings into decision-making.

“Every study presented at this colloquium should be assessed for actions that can be taken by the respective organisations. Do not let these studies become mere documents gathering dust on library shelves,” he said.

Wan Ahmad Dahlan also expressed hope that the proposed restructuring of INTAN, particularly efforts to strengthen its Research and Consultancy Centre, would enhance its capacity to conduct applied research addressing current challenges faced by government agencies.

The event also saw the launch of a book titled *Penyelidikan Sektor Awam Malaysia: Pendekatan Kajian Tindakan* (Malaysian Public Sector Research: An Action Research Approach), intended as a reference for civil servants and researchers seeking to promote impact-driven research.

The two-day colloquium, organised by the Public Service Department through INTAN in strategic collaboration with Universiti Utara Malaysia, brings together 800 participants and features 41 research papers across four key clusters: technology and digitalisation, economics, social issues and sustainability, and public policy. — Bernama
098e3cdbaded4e38: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 2 — Chang Cheng Hokkien Mee has closed it doors after 32 years of operation, but it still lives in the hearts of its patrons.
The stall, which was located in Chop Joo Hiong Eating House at Serangoon Avenue 3, served its last meal on Oct 31.

In an interview published by Shin Min Daily News yesterday, the hawkers, Wu Fushun, 64, and his wife Lin Rongduan, 61, said many old customers whom they hadn’t seen for many years came down after news of their coming closure spread.
Wu said customers surged by 50 per cent in the past week, and the couple said they were touched by the gifts they received from customers, including chocolates and handwritten cards.
They shared a thank-you letter written by an 11-year-old girl, the daughter of their longtime customers.
In the photo of the letter they shared to Shin Min Daily News, addressed to “uncle and auntie”, the girl said she was sad to see them go.

“Therefore, I wanted to write this letter to thank you. To some, this is just an ordinary little stall, but to me, it wasn’t just about delicious Hokkien mee, but also about the warm hospitality,” she wrote.

“I especially want to thank auntie, because every time I come, you always recognise me and are so kind, making me feel happy and warm. Thank you for your continued kindness and enthusiasm. I will miss your Hokkien mee and the warmth you brought me.”
She also wished them good health, peace, happiness and wished them the best for their future, signing of as “an 11-year-old girl who loves your Hokkien mee”.
Wu said his wife treasured the letter and brought it home as a keepsake.
He later shared they had been running the stall for six days a week for more than 10 hours a day for the past 32 years.
The long-term strain gradually took a toll on Wu’s health and they decided to close their doors to focus on their wellbeing. — AsiaOne

23c47c4155296590: KUALA LUMPUR: Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman (Muda-Muar) today defended the confidence and supply agreement (CSA) he signed with the government last week, saying it provides an avenue to push for two key institutional reforms.
He said the agreement was important not only to ensure fair and equitable constituency allocations for the MPs involved, but also to reduce the concentration of power in the prime minister's hands.
Under the CSA, the government vowed to limit the prime minister’s tenure and separate the roles of the attorney-general (AG) and public prosecutor before the end of its term.
Syed Saddiq said separating the AG and public prosecutor's roles would prevent the prime minister and Cabinet from controlling appointments to the top prosecution office.

"This would reduce the likelihood of corruption cases involving political allies being dropped, or the AG's Chambers or Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission being weaponised against political opponents," he told the Dewan Rakyat.
He said everyone, whether political allies or rivals, should be judged in court according to the facts and evidence of their case rather than the prime minister's influence.
The former Muda president was speaking during the committee stage debate on the 2027 budget.
Syed Saddiq signed the CSA with Putrajaya last week alongside six Bersatu MPs, led by party president Muhyiddin Yassin.
Perikatan Nasional MPs criticised the agreement, claiming it would stymie the seven opposition MPs from serving as checks and balances on the government.
Syed Saddiq said he had also supported the CSA signed between the Ismail Sabri Yaakob administration and Pakatan Harapan in September 2021.
He said the reforms proposed under the CSA should include enacting a law on the distribution of equal funds to all MPs before the parliamentary term expires.
Otherwise, he said the cycle of political revenge would continue, with opposition MPs barred from constituency development funds by the government.

0cacd9e7aeeb24e0: A designer named Marcin Wichary has revealed the story of how he freaked out a decent slab of the world’s Firefox-using population with Pac-Man.

Wichary has held senior design roles at Figma, Medium, and Google. As he wrote here, in 2010 Google decided to celebrate the 30th anniversary of Pac-Man by changing its logo at Google.com to a playable version of the game.

The Google of 2010 could still mention its motto of the time, “Don’t be evil,” without making anyone who heard it guffaw incredulously. The company’s frequent changes to the logo on its homepage – called Google Doodles, and which persist to this day – were still a notable part of net culture.
Wichary got the job of building the playable logo, and tweaking Pac-Man to replace its usual maze with a course that instead navigated around the letters GOOGLE.

“It was, frankly, a terrifying proposition,” Wichary wrote. “The homepage was then a very important destination, and my job title was only adjacent to ‘software engineer.’ But I started researching the game and recreating it all in HTML and CSS."
Google wanted a full Pac-Man experience, including sound, "because so many of Pac-Man’s sounds are beyond iconic: the starting melody, the waka-wakas, the death jingle."
Wichary began work before Google sought permission from Pac-Man’s owner Namco, because the search giant was “planning to wow them with a close-to-finished doodle.”
“The project was … going really well. I had fun coding the game and we seemed to have fun playing it. Namco eventually got onboard, too,” he wrote.
Google liked the game work so much, higher-ups decided it would be a great idea to have it start automatically if visitors to google.com stayed idle for ten seconds.

The designer liked that idea. “If there was anything scary about it at the time, it was only the thought of my code getting even more exposure – but I wasn’t worried about distraction, since the homepage was not a destination page you would ever linger on.”
What Google didn’t realise was that some people lingered on the home page without ever knowing they were there.
Those people used the Firefox browser with an extension called CoolPreviews that let users hover over a link to see a preview of a web page.
“The extension would quietly start at the same time Firefox was opened,” Wichary explained. “And it would immediately, in the background, invisibly and unbeknownst to the user, open a website.”
That website was Google’s home page, which now featured an auto-playing and version of Pac-Man that CoolPreviews users simply did not expect.

Which explained why, not long after setting the Pac-Man doodle live, Google received plenty of praise, but also reports about computers making strange noises due to CoolPreviews invisibly opening the noisy game.

“I pushed a patch within hours,” Wichary wrote, explaining that he added a mute button and a requirement to click something to make the game and its noises start. CoolPreviews couldn’t make those clicks, so the phantom Pac-Man sounds went away.

“Ironically, I don’t believe we ever heard of normal people being bothered by the autoplay – it seemed that indeed, few people stayed on the homepage for 10 seconds doing absolutely nothing,” Wichary wrote.

“The funny thing is that emergency live-patching [the] internet’s at the time most valuable homepage was perhaps the scariest part of that day for me, but that completely went over my sleep-deprived head,” he added.
Google changed Wichary’s title after this incident. His post shows an image describing him as “User experience designer. The Michael Bay of doodles.” ®
e9966eff88c22851: GEORGE TOWN, Nov 2 — DAP’s Air Putih assemblyman Lim Guan Eng has urged the Penang government to defer increases in land tax, water tariffs and other fees until the end of its term, saying the state’s improved financial position should allow it to avoid placing further pressure on residents and businesses.

Debating the 2027 Supply Bill and Development Estimates in the Penang State Legislative Assembly today, Lim said he supported the RM1.074 billion state budget, noting that the Consolidated Revenue Account balance had increased from RM522.87 million at the end of 2025 to RM651.28 million as at October 30 this year, while Penang’s gross domestic product grew 7.3 per cent to RM130.3 billion in 2025, compared with national growth of 5.2 per cent.

He said the budget’s theme, “Bringing the Vision Closer to the People and Forging a Legacy”, should translate into tangible benefits that would make life easier for the public, adding that the state should not risk losing public support by prioritising its legacy over people’s needs.
Lim also welcomed the appointment of new state secretary Datuk Dr Jafri Abdul Jalil, effective August 3, 2026, and thanked his predecessor Datuk Seri Zulkifli Long for his service.

Lim said ordinary people and micro, small and medium enterprises were facing challenging economic conditions and should not have to contend with higher taxes and compliance costs, pointing to land tax collections rising from RM116 million in both 2024 and 2025 to RM165 million as at September this year, an increase of RM49 million in nine months despite the payment deadline being extended to the end of 2026; he also cited national GDP growth of six per cent in the second quarter of 2026 and a 13.5 per cent increase in the banking sector’s pre-tax profits, from RM48.3 billion in 2024 to RM54.8 billion in 2025.

He also called on the state government to provide the remaining RM500,000 for road widening and safety improvements at Pintas Berani 5 near SJK(C) Kwang Hwa in Bagan Jermal, saying the RM1 million approved by Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming would widen the road from one lane to two and that the additional allocation was needed to improve safety for the school’s 1,118 pupils, teachers and other road users; he said the state only needed to contribute half the project’s remaining cost and that the funds had already been channelled to the Seberang Perai City Council.

On water supply, Lim urged the state government to table its bulk water supply agreement with Perak’s Prasarana Air dan Irigasi Perak Sdn Bhd in the state assembly for debate and approval, saying the 40-year arrangement from 2032 carried an estimated cost of RM24.6 billion up to 2072, comprising RM8.4 billion in infrastructure capacity charges and RM16.2 billion in water supply charges; he said the agreement should be made public and that the state should seek Perak’s consent to disclose its terms even if a non-disclosure agreement was in place, as Penang residents would ultimately bear the cost.

Lim also proposed an independent state commission of inquiry into the October 25 slope collapse at Taman Seri Rambai, Paya Terubong, which killed 73-year-old doctor Wong Kar Lin and led to the immediate evacuation of six nearby homes, saying those responsible should be held accountable; he disputed claims that the project had been approved during his tenure as chief minister from 2008 to 2018, stating that planning permission was granted in 2023 and earthworks and building plans in 2024, when he was no longer chief minister or finance minister, and said the allegations had been circulated on eight websites and referred to his lawyer for legal action.

Turning to the proposed 70-acre reclamation project off Persiaran Karpal Singh, estimated to cost RM1 billion, and the agreement to rehabilitate the 84-acre Jelutong landfill, Lim questioned why the agreement had not been cancelled after the contractor’s applications were rejected five times by the Department of Environment, despite an October 18 deadline set by the chief minister; he also asked why extensions had been granted for more than six years since the agreement was signed on February 21, 2020, how much the contractor still owed the Penang Development Corporation and state government, and why the reclamation project was proceeding without a signed agreement.

Citing the Auditor-General’s Report 2026, Lim criticised the Penang Development Corporation’s handling of the Jalan Perusahaan-Jalan Tok Kangar road and bridge upgrading project, saying the combined cost of RM63.4 million for its two phases — RM10.6 million for Phase 1 and RM52.8 million for Phase 2 — was RM20.4 million, or 47 per cent, above the original RM43 million estimate; he said the audit found that Phase 2 had taken more than seven years after its open tender was awarded on July 12, 2019, that delays reached 2,278 days and that RM3.12 million in progress payments had been made to a replacement contractor before a formal contract was signed, while PDC had still received a six-month bonus for 2024, paid in February 2025.

He also questioned PDC’s ability to undertake the proposed 1,142-acre Batu Kawan Industrial Park 2 development, of which 872 acres would be available for investors, asking whether the project should instead be opened to private-sector participation; Lim cited the sale of 559 acres of PDC land at Byram, Batu Kawan, for RM646 million through a direct deal without an open tender, compared with a subsequent open request for proposal offering RM818 million, or RM172 million more, and argued that a private-sector partnership could bring in funds sooner and accelerate development.

On economic prospects, Lim said Penang and Malaysia had benefited from geopolitical and economic tensions between the United States and China, as well as the impact of US President Donald Trump’s tariffs, with foreign investment and exports reaching record levels, particularly in electronics; he welcomed the federal government’s RM100 million allocation approved by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim for the Penang Technology Financial Centre, which he said could build on the state’s technological strengths in digital development, artificial intelligence and new forms of trade.

However, Lim said economic growth was uneven and some sectors continued to face difficulties, calling for a separate Special Financial Zone to attract foreign funds and activities involving cryptocurrency, fintech and digital finance, which he said fell outside the Penang Technology Financial Centre’s focus on technology, start-ups and AI; he proposed a 40-hectare site at Ampang Jajar between the Bagan and Permatang Pauh parliamentary constituencies, near public transport links including the planned LRT station at Penang Sentral, expected to be completed in 2032, saying this would help balance development between Penang island and Seberang Perai.

9599351855eb062d: Despite the US president’s ratings being at rock bottom, undoing his legacy will be difficult, not least because the Democrats are in disarray The stats and polling all suggest one thing: the Republicans are set for a hammering in the midterms. Donald Trump has the lowest approval rating of any US president going into a midterm election since Harry Truman. And it’s still dropping. The Democrats are projected to win by a margin of 11 percentage points, the largest swing by any party in almost 20 years. It is possible that the Democrats flip the Senate and secure a large majority in Congress. Those majorities would make a material difference, perhaps finally establishing oversight of the policies Trump has brought in during his second term: immigration enforcement, trade disputes, gutting the federal workforce, the Iran war, to say nothing of his own family’s corruption. The tide seems to be turning, and one question is on everyone’s mind: is the Trump era really ending? “Nobody wants to jinx it,” wrote David Wallace-Wells of the New York Times, but: “All the signs we have suggest that, historic or not, these midterms are likely to mark the end of a political era.” What that gives way to is a much more complicated picture in which the US will be delivered from Trump himself, but remains a country riven and undermined by what he has unleashed. By the time he is gone, Trump will have been president for eight years, and a toxic force for more than 12. That is a long time even for a normal politician. Under one who shatters norms and forces himself into the centre of everything, Trump’s effect is as if he were president for decades. Continue reading...
6e034b853ef95a2d: GEORGE TOWN, Nov 2 — The state government is still conducting a conceptual design study for the proposed Penang Third Link Bridge as an alternative to the undersea tunnel, before presenting it to the Penang Port Commission (PPC) for feedback.

State Infrastructure, Transport and Digital Committee chairman Zairil Khir Johari said the state government had approved a realignment study based on a bridge design concept, taking into consideration plans to expand Penang Port and the need to ease traffic congestion in Gurney Bay and its surrounding areas.

He said the proposed realignment involved shifting the route northwards to ensure it was compatible with Penang Port's expansion plans, while avoiding any disruption to port operations and vessel navigation routes.
“At present, the conceptual design study is underway, and its findings will be presented to the PPC for feedback and further consideration.

“This assessment aims to ensure that any decision on the project's implementation takes into account technical feasibility, financial implications, people's mobility needs, shipping safety and marine navigation, as well as the long-term benefits to the state's socioeconomic development,” he said.

He said this in response to a question from Teh Lai Heng (PH-Komtar) on the latest status, as of September 2026, of the three highway projects and one undersea tunnel project, during the state assembly sitting here today.
The proposed 6.5-kilometre undersea tunnel linking Gurney Drive to Bagan Ajam on the mainland is part of the Penang Transport Master Plan (PTMP).

On the North Coastal Paired Road (NCPR) project, Zairil said the state government was reviewing part of the proposed alignment, covering the route from Tanjung Bungah to Teluk Bahang, to ensure that it took into account technical suitability, local sensitivities, population density and the risk of soil erosion.
In this regard, he said the terms of the Sub-Agreement (SA) were being finalised before it could be signed.

“At the same time, the state government is also undertaking an Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) for part of the new alignment to ensure that the proposed development takes into account transportation needs, safety and the interests of local residents,” he said.

The NCPR project is part of a package involving three major roads and a tunnel, which was awarded in 2013. It involves the construction of a 10.61-kilometre highway, comprising an 8.41-kilometre land route and a 2.2-kilometre coastal viaduct linking Tanjung Bungah and Teluk Bahang.

Construction is expected to begin in 2026 and be completed by 2031. Upon completion, travel time between Tanjung Bungah and Teluk Bahang is expected to be reduced from 30 to 45 minutes during peak hours to just seven minutes. — Bernama
89d67b8c81715ec5: KUALA LUMPUR: A director and a former director of a company operating a dessert cafe were charged in the sessions court here with using the term "franchise" without registration approval.

Choco Loco (M) Sdn Bhd director Syaidatul Natasha Suhaimi, 36, and former director Hadi Asasa, 37, are jointly charged over two franchise agreements between Choco Loco and two other firms: Chocolate Cravings Sdn Bhd and Choco Rush Global Trading Sdn Bhd.

They allegedly committed the offences at Solaris Dutamas on April 1, 2021 and June 1, 2021, by using the term "franchise" in agreements with both companies without obtaining approval from the registrar of franchises under Section 8 of the Franchise Act 1998.
The two charges of holding out as a franchise were framed under Section 37A of the Act, punishable under Section 37A(b), read with Section 34 of the Penal Code.
If convicted, they each face a maximum RM100,000 fine, up to one year in prison or both.
Choco Loco itself faces two similar charges under Section 37A(a) of the Act, which carries a maximum fine of RM250,000 for the first offence and up to RM500,000 for every subsequent offence.
The duo claimed trial to their charges, while Syaidatul pleaded not guilty on behalf of the company before judge Siti Shakirah Mohtarudin.
The court allowed joint bail of RM16,000 for all charges.
Lawyer Kausar Khairi represented the accused, while prosecuting officer Sallim Wahid appeared for the prosecution.
e039710e8a268911: KOTA BHARU, Nov 2 — The Kelantan government allocated more than RM10.86 million for house repair works and the provision of building materials to poor and underprivileged households in the state in 2024 and 2025.

Menteri Besar Datuk Mohd Nassuruddin Daud said a total of 1,034 assistance packages were provided during the period under the Dhuafa’ Housing Assistance programme implemented by the Kelantan State Development Office.
He said of the total, 473 assistance packages were provided in 2024, involving an expenditure of RM5.04 million, while 561 were channelled in 2025, involving an allocation of RM5.811 million.
“The assistance covers house repair works and the provision of building materials, based on the needs and extent of damage to the homes of eligible recipients,” he said.
He said this in reply to a question from Mohd Azmawi Fikri Abdul Ghani (BN-Nenggiri) during the state assembly sitting at the Kota Darulnaim Complex here today.

Elaborating further, Mohd Nassuruddin said the selection of aid recipients was carried out through an application, investigation and verification process by the Land and District offices, subject to eligibility requirements and the availability of funds.
In addition to house repair assistance and contributions of building materials, the state government also provides 180 new houses annually throughout Kelantan under the same programme.
“Each house is valued at RM65,000, with a total allocation of approximately RM11.7 million annually. Insya-Allah, we will be able to assist more people in need,” he said. — Bernama
1ebc207cc9fe8d09: HONG KONG: BYD, China’s biggest carmaker, reported higher sales for the sixth straight month as exports made up for slumping demand at home.

BYD’s October passenger vehicles sales climbed 11% as exports doubled and local deliveries fell, according to a statement on Sunday. Chery Automobile, the nation’s biggest exporter, reported sales increased 5%, with exports climbing by 60%.

Shares of BYD and Chery rose in Hong Kong trading on Monday as the continued strength of overseas demand for Chinese cars helped ease concerns about the prolonged downturn in their home market. Still, export growth hasn’t necessarily impressed investors as BYD last week reported earnings and revenue that missed analyst estimates.

Among other automakers, Geely’s overseas sales more than doubled, allowing it to squeeze out a 1% gain in total deliveries. Xiaomi and Xpeng’s monthly sales surpassed 50,000, while Zhejiang Leapmotor Technology delivered more than 100,000 vehicles for a fourth consecutive month.
Meanwhile, Seres Group, the maker of Aito cars, posted a 50% decline in sales, while Li Auto’s monthly deliveries dropped by 9%.
c04e28271c0b30f7: KUALA LUMPUR: Seorang Ahli Parlimen Perikatan Nasional (PN) mempersoalkan perjanjian keyakinan dan perbekalan (CSA) antara tujuh Ahli Parlimen pembangkang dengan Putrajaya kerana ia tidak perlu memandangkan blok kerajaan mempunyai majoriti dua pertiga di Dewan Rakyat.
Ronald Kiandee (PN-Beluran) berkata, kerajaan mempunyai jumlah kerusi mencukupi untuk meluluskan rang undang-undang, termasuk pindaan Perlembagaan yang memerlukan sokongan majoriti dua pertiga.
Naib presiden Bersatu yang digantung keahliannya berkata, CSA lazimnya dimeterai kerajaan minoriti yang tiada sokongan mencukupi untuk meluluskan rang undang-undang.
"Ini situasi di bawah kerajaan (Ismail Sabri Yaakob), apabila ia memang tidak mempunyai sokongan majoriti mencukupi.
"Namun, kerajaan sekarang bukan saja mempunyai majoriti selesa, malah menguasai majoriti dua pertiga," katanya ketika membahas Belanjawan 2027 di peringkat jawatankuasa.

Pentadbiran Ismail mempunyai majoriti mudah, tetapi perdana menteri ketika itu menandatangani memorandum persefahaman transformasi dan kestabilan politik dengan Pakatan Harapan bagi menjamin kestabilan kerajaan sehingga tamat penggal Parlimen.

Minggu lalu, Presiden Bersatu, Muhyiddin Yassin (PN-Pagoh) mengetuai lima Ahli Parlimen lain parti itu menandatangani CSA dengan kerajaan. Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman (Muda-Muar) turut menandatangani perjanjian berkenaan.
Di bawah perjanjian itu, Ahli Parlimen terbabit akan menyokong kerajaan sehingga tamat penggal pentadbirannya.

Sebagai balasan, Ahli Parlimen pembangkang mendapat akses peruntukan pembangunan kawasan, manakala Putrajaya akan berusaha mengehadkan tempoh jawatan perdana menteri serta memisahkan peranan peguam negara dan pendakwa raya sebelum penggal pentadbirannya berakhir.
Kiandee berkata, CSA itu memberi gambaran seolah-olah kerajaan tidak stabil dan memerlukan sokongan tambahan daripada Ahli Parlimen pembangkang.
Beliau turut memberi amaran langkah itu boleh menimbulkan persepsi Putrajaya menggunakan janji dana pembangunan kawasan di bawah CSA sebagai senjata politik untuk meraih sokongan tambahan.
"Kerajaan tidak patut menggunakan kuasa, pengaruh atau kelebihan jumlah sokongan untuk menjadikan peruntukan Parlimen sebagai senjata politik. Perkara ini tidak patut berlaku."
CSA itu dimeterai ketika hubungan PH dan Barisan Nasional, rakan sekutu utama dalam kerajaan persekutuan, semakin tegang.
Pada masa sama, Bersatu kekal komponen PN, tetapi hubungannya dengan PAS yang menerajui gabungan pembangkang itu semakin renggang.
698f4a54de269143: PETALING JAYA: PKR mendesak Ketua Menteri Melaka Ab Rauf Yusoh menjelaskan status terkini 55 projek pembangunan negeri yang dilaporkan masih belum bermula tahun lalu.
Timbalan Setiausaha Agung PKR, Sivamalar Genapathy, berkata penjelasan itu perlu diberikan sebelum pentadbiran Rauf meminta mandat baharu daripada rakyat Melaka.
“Jika projek-projek tersebut sudah siap, tunjukkan hasilnya kepada rakyat. Jika masih tertangguh, jelaskan puncanya dan bentangkan pelan penyelesaiannya,” katanya dalam kenyataan.
Pada 10 Jun 2025, Rauf dilaporkan berkata daripada 241 projek pembangunan negeri, 86 telah siap, 100 sedang dilaksanakan dan 55 lagi belum bermula.
Ketika itu, sebanyak RM19.52 juta atau 22.18% daripada peruntukan pembangunan negeri berjumlah RM88 juta dibelanjakan sehingga 31 Mei.
Sivamalar berkata, rakyat kini wajar diberi gambaran terkini selepas hampir 17 bulan.
“Adakah semua 55 projek itu kini telah dimulakan? Berapa yang sudah siap? Berapa yang masih tertangguh?” soalnya.
Beliau turut menggesa kerajaan negeri menerbitkan butiran projek terbabit, termasuk lokasi, nilai peruntukan, agensi pelaksana, status semasa dan sasaran penyiapan.
Menurutnya, kedudukan peruntukan yang diluluskan, disalurkan dan dibelanjakan juga perlu diperincikan bagi membolehkan prestasi pelaksanaan dinilai berdasarkan fakta.
Sivamalar mengakui projek pembangunan boleh terjejas akibat isu perolehan, kelulusan teknikal, tanah, kontraktor atau kelewatan penyaluran dana.
Bagaimanapun, katanya, sebarang kelewatan perlu disertai penjelasan dan langkah penyelesaian yang jelas.
“Rakyat tidak hidup dengan angka dalam laporan semata-mata. Mereka mahu melihat hasil pembangunan yang benar-benar dapat dinikmati.
“Mandat baharu mesti diraih melalui rekod prestasi yang boleh disemak, bukan sekadar janji yang diulang,” katanya.
14a26293aa90021e: PETALING JAYA: A PKR leader has urged Melaka chief minister Ab Rauf Yusoh to provide an update on the status of 55 projects that had yet to commence construction as of June last year.
PKR deputy secretary-general G Sivamalar asked whether these projects had progressed over the past 17 months, saying Rauf should issue the update before seeking a new mandate from voters.
She called for the state government to list all 55 projects as well as their locations, value, implementing agency, original project schedule and latest targeted completion date.
"The people deserve to know what projects have been completed and which ones are delayed, and why.

"These 55 projects could comprise public facilities long awaited by residents, infrastructure desperately needed by local communities, and developments meant to benefit the people of Melaka," she said in a statement.

Sivamalar said it was crucial that the Barisan Nasional (BN) state government exercise prudence and responsibility in managing public finances by ensuring that development allocations yield results felt by the people.
"Before BN seeks another five-year mandate from the people, Rauf's administration needs to openly prove its record of achievements.
"The people deserve to evaluate BN based on the results, not just project announcements, allocation figures or political promises," she added.
In June 2025, Rauf said 22.18% of the state's RM88 million development allocation for that year had been spent.
The chief minister said this covered expenditure on 241 projects, including 86 that were completed and 100 that were still in progress. Another 55 had yet to commence at the time.
BN said that Rauf would continue serving as chief minister should the coalition form the state government again.
4a5777a783929b68: SAN FRANCISCO: John Ternus will host his first earnings call as Apple's CEO on Monday, with investors looking to the company's forecast to determine whether a blitz of new products can help offset rising costs for memory chips.

Ternus, who took the reins from Tim Cook in September, has overseen the introduction of Apple's first foldable phone, smart home hub and touch-screen laptops. All of those products began shipping during the company's current fiscal first quarter, amid what Cook had called a "100-year flood" of rising memory costs.

Apple will face scrutiny over three key issues: its crucial holiday-quarter outlook, Ternus' remarks on AI and the revamped Siri, and rising memory-chip costs that analysts expect to drag quarterly profit growth to its weakest in six quarters.
Apple has been trying to position its AI offerings differently than rivals such as Meta Platforms' Muse agent, which took App Store rankings by storm in recent weeks.

Rivals such as OpenAI, which Apple is suing over alleged trade-secret theft, are also developing devices aimed at displacing the iPhone as the central device in people's lives. How Apple embraces AI could also have large implications for the future of its services business, whose slowing growth has worried investors after years of rapid expansion.

"Recent agentic innovation far outpaces our experience with Siri AI, but Apple has acknowledged that Siri AI ... is far more focused on trust/privacy," said Dan Morgan, portfolio manager at Synovus Trust, which owns Apple shares.
Apple is marketing Apple's AI systems toward "everyday people" rather than Silicon Valley insiders, who are big users of frontier AI models from the likes of OpenAI.
Morgan added that investors want to know whether Apple could profit by distributing third-party AI agents through its App Store and taking a cut of the business they generate.

For now, Apple's reluctance to join the massive AI spending race has worked in its favor. Its shares have risen about 27% this year, outperforming tech giants such as Microsoft, Alphabet, Meta and Amazon as investors seek shelter from mounting concerns over the cost of building AI infrastructure.

Analysts expect Apple to report a nearly 11% rise in revenue to US$113.39 billion for the July-September period, the company's fiscal fourth quarter, according to LSEG data. Net profit is expected to rise about 6% to US$29.04 billion.
Apple's services business is expected to grow almost 10% to US$31.56 billion, its slowest pace in more than three years.

iPhone sales are projected to climb about 15% to US$56.54 billion, slowing from growth of about 22% in the previous three months. The results will capture just nine days of sales of the new iPhone 18 Pro models, while the iPhone Duo, the firm's first foldable, came out on Oct 23, which will benefit the holiday quarter.

Remarks on how the Duo is selling will be scrutinized after some buyers of the device that starts at US$1,999 in the US have reported cracks and lines along the inner display's central fold, prompting Apple to offer replacements. Duo's online orders had sold out within minutes.

IDC analyst Nabila Popal said she expects demand for the Duo to continue exceeding supply despite the screen problems. The test will be how quickly Apple can replace affected devices while supplies remain tight, she said.
Bank of America estimates Duo buyers face average delivery waits of 79 days, with shipments stretching into January.
d6abf4fdcfdc64b9: KUALA LUMPUR: Kementerian Kesihatan (KKM) merampas pelbagai ubat kawalan berat badan dan anti diabetes tidak berdaftar termasuk ubat percubaan Retatrutide serta produk tular Ozempic bernilai lebih RM400,000 yang dijual secara haram dalam talian bagi tempoh 2025 hingga September lepas.

Menteri Kesihatan, Dzulkefly Ahmad, berkata tindakan itu diambil susulan peningkatan trend pembekalan dan pembelian ubat-ubatan glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1 RA) tanpa pemantauan klinikal dan kawalan sah pihak berkuasa.

"Bagi tempoh 2025 sehingga September 2026, sebanyak 12 serbuan berkaitan Retatrutide telah dilaksanakan secara rampasan 697 unit melibatkan RM341,000. Retatrutide adalah satu yang saya kira belum lagi dalam formulari kami.

"Bahagian Penguatkuasaan Farmasi juga mengesan penjualan ubat Ozempic, (mengandungi bahan aktif Semaglutide) secara tidak sah. Bagi tempoh 2025 hingga September 2026, tujuh serbuan berkaitan produk ini dilaksanakan dengan rampasan berjumlah 62 unit melibatkan RM64,170," katanya pada sesi soal jawab di Dewan Rakyat hari ini.

Beliau berkata demikian bagi menjawab soalan tambahan Dr Zaliha Mustafa (PH-Sekijang) mengenai tindakan KKM dalam mengawal fenomena penjualan ubatan berkenaan dalam talian tanpa kawalan di Dewan Rakyat hari ini.

Dzulkefly berkata KKM menerusi Bahagian Penguatkuasaan Farmasi melaksanakan pemantauan dan penguatkuasaan berterusan bagi mengekang aktiviti penjualan tidak sah yang dipromosikan menerusi platform e-dagang dan media sosial.
"Kita akan terus memantau secara lebih tegas penyalahgunaan e-dagang dan e-platform ini, sebab pada akhirnya yang kita mahu jaga adalah keselamatan dan nyawa rakyat," katanya.

Menjawab soalan asal Ramkarpal mengenai jumlah dana bagi rawatan GLP-1 RA di bawah Belanjawan 2026, Dzulkefly berkata buat masa ini tiada peruntukan khusus bagi rawatan ubat GLP-1 seperti Ozempic, Tirzepatide dan Mounjaro.
Bagaimanapun, pesakit yang memerlukan boleh memohon menerusi Unit Ubat Kelulusan Khas (UKK) KKM menggunakan peruntukan sedia ada.
"Untuk rekod, sebanyak 240 permohonan rawatan telah diluluskan bagi tempoh Januari hingga September 2026 melibatkan kos keseluruhan RM2.56 juta," katanya.
Selain itu, beliau berkata KKM akan terus mengemukakan permohonan peruntukan khusus untuk perolehan GLP-1 pada masa hadapan.

Sementara itu, Dzulkefly berkata KKM dalam proses akhir memuktamadkan draf peraturan baharu berkaitan sistem penggredan Nutri-Grade (pengelasan nutrisi makanan) secara mandatori berasaskan kepada kandungan jumlah gula dalam minuman sebelum dikemukakan kepada Jabatan Peguam Negara (AGC) menjelang November 2026.
Beliau berkata inisiatif itu dilaksanakan melalui proses pindaan di bawah Peraturan-Peraturan Makanan 1985 bagi membantu pengguna membuat pilihan makanan dan minuman yang lebih sihat.
Beliau berkata demikian bagi menjawab soalan Dr Kelvin Yii Lee Wuen (PH-Bandar Kuching) mengenai pendekatan komprehensif KKM menangani penyakit tidak berjangkit (NCD).
7519732eb7b4dd08: WASHINGTON: Democrats teed up final get-out-the-vote rallies Monday on the eve of midterm elections where they expect to win at least partial control of Congress and impose political constraints on president Donald Trump for the first time in two years.
Rallies - including by star Democratic Senate candidates James Talarico in Texas and Adam Hamilton in Kansas - were capping a campaign of breathtaking tension and bitterness.

For his closing argument, Trump chose a speech in Washington at the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool - a landmark that has become synonymous with the 80-year-old president's obsessive, controversial drive to redevelop the US capital.
"We're going to win," he said on Sunday.
Polls, however, show that Democrats are near certain to take the majority from Republicans in the House of Representatives and have a real shot at winning the currently Republican Senate.

Even winning just the House would mean Democrats have voting power over the federal budget and would lead powerful committees able to investigate alleged corruption under Trump, the Epstein files and other explosive issues.

The loss of total Republican dominance would push Trump into unfamiliar and uncomfortable territory: a lame-duck period beset with high inflation at home, the sputtering war against Iran and hostile Democratic investigations into his activities in Washington.
But a decade into the Trump era, Democrats remain wary about predictions of victory.
"Nauseously optimistic," Democratic Senator Raphael Warnock told CNN to describe the mood.
Scorched earth

Republicans led by Trump have fought a political scorched-earth campaign, painting Democrats as communists and openly branding Abdul El-Sayed, a Muslim candidate for senator in Michigan, as a terrorist.
Addressing a crowd in Iowa on Sunday, Trump said Democrats are "extreme and dangerous radicals" who will "steal your wealth" and let in migrants to "ransack, rape and plunder."
But polls show Americans heavily souring on Trump's wrecking-ball act.
An NBC News poll released on Sunday showed 60% disapprove of his performance, particularly over high prices exacerbated by his now eight-month war against Iran.
While the House seems highly likely to turn Democratic, the battle for the Senate is up in the air.
Only a third of the Senate's 100 seats are being contested in these midterms, and few of the races were seen as favourable to Democrats.
However, with surprisingly strong challenges in deeply Republican states, pollsters now say the odds of a Democratic flip are at minimum even.
The final New York Times/Siena poll released Sunday evening showed Democratic candidates leading in all seven seats viewed as most competitive, though five remained within the margin of error.
A Democratic Senate would be able to shut down Trump's lifetime appointments to courts - especially the Supreme Court.
While Tuesday is election day, early voting has already seen a record 54 million people cast ballots around the country.
The midterms have seen about US$11 billion spent on advertising, with large chunks coming from individual mega-donors.
Elon Musk, a close Trump ally who led the so-called DOGE effort in dismantling entire government departments, has given a staggering nearly half-billion dollars to help get Republicans elected.
6fc9d5fcf1d3420b: Inkpen and Combe, Berkshire: If the price goes down, the village WhatsApp group lights up Beyond the reach of the gas mains, there is tension about the coming winter. 6a5dde3e74ccb608: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 2 — Bukit Aman will submit its investigation papers into the death of detainee Noorizwan Zulkefly at the Cheras district police headquarters lock-up to the Attorney General's Chambers (AGC) on Wednesday, along with its recommendations.

Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department (CID) director Datuk M. Kumar said the investigation, which was recently taken over by the department, was being conducted under Section 331 of the Penal Code.
He said police would await further instructions and advice from the AGC after submitting the investigation papers.
Kumar also confirmed that the detainee had sustained significant physical injuries, which a forensic pathologist had verified were not self-inflicted.
However, he said the cause of death remained under investigation, and police could not yet establish whether the injuries had contributed to Noorizwan's death.

“What I can confirm is that there were physical injuries, which were confirmed by a specialist forensic pathologist, and they were not self-inflicted,” he told a press conference at Menara 2 Bukit Aman here.
Separately, Kumar confirmed that police had received a report lodged by a doctor involved in the case over alleged harassment.

He said investigations were being conducted under three provisions of the Penal Code, namely Section 506 for criminal intimidation, Section 186 for voluntarily obstructing a public servant in the discharge of their duties, and Section 189.
Kumar said investigations into the doctor's report were ongoing and further developments would be announced.
Noorizwan, 42, died on October 1 while in custody at the Cheras district police headquarters lock-up.
News reports quoting family members and their lawyers indicated that Noorizwan had sustained nearly two dozen severe injuries, based on preliminary postmortem findings.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has ordered a thorough, transparent and uncompromising investigation into Noorizwan's death in police custody.

Bukit Aman had classified the case under Section 331 following a statement recorded from a forensic medical consultant at Hospital Canselor Tuanku Muhriz who conducted the postmortem, Kumar was previously quoted as saying.
The consultant confirmed signs of external injuries on several parts of the deceased's body that were consistent with blunt-force trauma and were not self-inflicted, Kumar said.
The case has since drawn national attention and renewed public scrutiny of the government's pledge to reform detention procedures and end custodial deaths.
Addressing Parliament last week, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail pledged transparency in the investigation and said officers found responsible would be punished.
38ccc4869196d22d: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 2 — Police arrested 282 people and seized RM32,149 in cash during a nationwide crackdown on online gambling and unlicensed lottery operations involving 201 business premises over the weekend.

Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department (CID) director Datuk M. Kumar said the two-day operation, dubbed Ops Dadu Khas, was conducted from October 31 to November 1 across the country, including Sabah and Sarawak.
He said 201 raids were carried out, comprising 108 premises linked to online gambling activities and 93 involving unlicensed public lottery operations.
“The 282 individuals arrested were aged between 20 and 65, comprising 229 men and 53 women.

“Of these, 223 were Malaysians while the remaining 59 were foreign nationals from Indonesia, Myanmar, Nepal and Bangladesh, who had been employed by local syndicates,” he said at a press conference at Menara 2 Bukit Aman here.
Kumar said the police also seized various equipment and electronic devices believed to have been used in the illegal gambling operations, including tablets, mobile phones and mobile printers.
He said all those arrested had been remanded for between one and four days to assist investigations and help identify the masterminds behind the activities.
Kumar said preliminary investigations had identified several syndicates operating under names including Winbox and Alibaba, with police working to identify their leaders.

He added that investigations would also be conducted under the Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act 2001 (AMLA), as offences under the Common Gaming Houses Act 1953 could serve as predicate offences for money laundering investigations.

Kumar said the police would also recommend that electricity supplies to all 201 premises be disconnected after investigations were completed, in accordance with Section 21A of the Common Gaming Houses Act 1953.
He said the syndicates often moved between premises to evade detection, using business establishments such as cafes, beverage outlets and sundry shops as fronts for their online gambling operations.

“They may operate at location A today, close it tomorrow and move to location B. This is because their operations are conducted online, with transactions also carried out online, allowing them to operate from virtually anywhere,” he said.

Kumar said the police had been conducting intelligence-gathering operations to identify the premises involved and would recommend enforcement action to the relevant local authorities once sufficient evidence had been gathered.

b91bd7f46fe98089: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 2 — Some Malaysian firms remain reluctant to pay local vocational graduates decent wages, often offering them salaries equivalent to those of foreign workers despite recent increases to the national minimum wage, Parliament was told this morning.

Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani said this reflected a broader unwillingness among businesses to move away from relying on cheap foreign labour as a core business model, even as policymakers introduce incentives and impose quotas to encourage companies to innovate.
“Unfortunately, some of these companies want to pay these TVET (technical and vocational education and training) graduates at the rate of foreign workers,” he said during Question Time.
“When we increased our minimum salary to RM1,700, it still wasn’t enough. Why? Because they pay those with TVET qualifications or these TVET students the same salary as foreign workers,” he added.

Malaysia has produced around 400,000 local TVET graduates in an effort to curb the nation's reliance on migrant labour, but many established domestic firms continue to offer starting salaries at the statutory minimum wage of RM1,700 a month, regardless of technical qualifications.

While migrant workers often receive employer-provided accommodation, Johari said local technicians with TVET qualifications are paid equivalent basic wages but have to cover their own rental expenses.
He acknowledged that poor policies were partly to blame.
“On top of that, they place them inside foreign worker housing areas, yet they have to pay rent outside of those accommodation areas,” he said.

59704ddc8a95d50f: As debate and legal argument continue over the extent to which developers of large language models are entitled to feed the world’s data into their systems without paying for it, India’s government has come up with an idea to regulate and secure the flow of information.
India’s motive is to create AI models trained on local data, because it thinks offshore model-makers won’t be motivated to address the nation’s issues or to ensure owners of data stay in control.
The scheme India’s Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) thinks can make that happen is called the “Data Empowerment and Protection Architecture (DEPA) for AI Training.”
As described by Professor Ajay Kumar Sood, Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government of India, DEPA means “the model travels to the data, rather than the data travelling to the model.”

The scheme envisions “Training Data Providers” (TDPs) – examples of which include hospitals, banks, and government agencies – sharing anonymized and encrypted data with a “Data Exchange Platform” (DEP).
Entities called “Training Data Consumers” (TDCs) access the data stored at the DEPs to train their models.

DEPs will operate what MeitY calls “hardware-based Secure Data Environments” in which “data remains encrypted and isolated even during processing.” They also enforce rules set by TDPs that describe how TDCs can use data.

MeitY’s DEPA framework [PDF] says this scheme means “Differential privacy techniques are systematically applied to prevent the model from learning or revealing individual specific information,” adding “All activities inside the secure data environments are immutably logged for audit purposes, ensuring that the process is both secure and transparent.”
India’s government already operates several data exchanges, but it is unclear how much work remains to make DEPA a reality.

Once DEPA is working, MeitY envisions model-makers will use it to do things like “unlock currently fragmented health data to power breakthroughs in AI-driven diagnostics, drug discovery, and public health management.”

The optimism extends to financial services. India is home to literally thousands of banks, and MeitY thinks “DEPA can enable secure sharing of diverse financial data, potentially extending formal credit to 400 million underserved individuals and MSMEs and fueling next-generation fintech innovation.”
India’s government has long believed that if financial services companies can lend to more people, it will boost economic development.

“Similarly, in Education, DEPA can overcome data interoperability challenges to enable AI-powered personalized learning for millions and create portable skill credentials essential for a future-ready workforce of its 250 million students in a $29 billion EdTech sector,” the framework states. “The successful adoption of DEPA Training across these domains is the essential catalyst for realizing India’s vision of inclusive growth and responsible AI leadership on the global stage.”
While the purpose of the framework is to build Indian AIs for Indians, the document also has half an eye on the nation’s international standing.

“DEPA is India’s contribution to global science diplomacy, advancing the efforts of institutions such as the World Bank and the United Nations to shape a more inclusive and responsible global AI ecosystem,” the framework states.

It also makes several mentions of digital public infrastructure (DPI), an idea pioneered by India that involves government funding creation of tools like the Unified Payments Interface payment systems and the Bharat Taxi zero-commission ride-sharing platform, to ensure Big Tech companies don’t dominate the local market.
India also uses its DPI as a diplomatic tool, by giving it away to friendly nations. ®

ab4e52d26d0d3d17: WASHINGTON, Nov 2 — A federal judge yesterday tossed out an extremely unusual attempt by US President Donald Trump’s administration to hold up midterm election results in Alaska should the Democratic Senate candidate win.
The judge dismissed the closely watched lawsuit, saying it would be unworkable.

The Department of Justice (DOJ) had asked the court to block certification of the results if incumbent Republican Dan Sullivan loses tomorrow, because a second candidate also named Dan Sullivan would have drawn away votes.
The legal bid, which Trump has said he ordered personally, sparked alarm, given concerns that Republicans will seek to contest losses in the midterms battle for control of Congress.
Alaska is one of the states where Democrats are aiming to flip Republican-held seats in their uphill bid to win the Senate majority.

According to Trump and the lawsuit, the Democratic candidate in Alaska, Mary Peltola, has tried to get an unfair advantage by recruiting another person named Sullivan to run and confuse voters who intended to back the incumbent Republican Senator Sullivan.
They sought to force an investigation if the Democrat wins to check how many voters who cast ballots for the second Sullivan actually meant to choose the Republican incumbent.

Such an attempt “would likely result in voter ‘confusion and consequent incentive to remain away from the polls.’ Such late-breaking changes to the election rules are strongly disfavored,” said the ruling by Judge Sharon Gleason, an appointee of former Democratic president Barack Obama.
Peltola has denied deliberately recruiting the second Sullivan into the race.
Shortly after Gleason’s ruling, the DOJ stated it plans to file an appeal.
“Alaskan voters deserve a fair election, not to be misled in an attempt to rig outcomes,” the DOJ said through its rapid response account on X.

9f2224bb9e6f9e84: WASHINGTON, Nov 2 — Republicans made a final push yesterday to prevent a predicted thumping in US midterm elections where Democrats are gunning to win Congress and impose a first political check on President Donald Trump’s unprecedented pursuit of power.
Polls show Democrats are all but certain to take the majority from Republicans in the House of Representatives in tomorrow’s vote and have a shot at winning the Senate.
But after a decade of Trump defying political gravity and two years of a second presidency in which he has ridden roughshod over every norm, Democrats remain nervous.
“Nauseously optimistic,” Democratic Senator Raphael Warnock told CNN to describe the mood.

Those jitters increased Sunday over an ugly party rift in Michigan, a key battleground where a Democratic congresswoman defected to back Republican Mike Rogers against the Democratic candidate Abdul El-Sayed.
The consensus among analysts, however, is that Democrats are surging.

Trump headlined the Republicans’ last-ditch charge, holding rallies for candidates in Iowa and Kansas — states where ordinarily his party should be confident of victory and not require presidential boosts.
Along with making lurid claims that Democrats will turn the country communist, Trump is dangling the promise of US$5,000 (RM20,329) payments to everyone in the country if his party wins.
“We’re going to win,” he told the crowd in Iowa, painting Democrats as “extreme and dangerous radicals” who will “steal your wealth” and let in migrants to “ransack, rape and plunder.”
But polls show Americans have soured on Trump’s wrecking-ball presidency.
An NBC News poll released Sunday showed 60 percent disapprove of Trump’s performance, particularly over high prices exacerbated by his now eight-month, sputtering war against Iran.
Curbing Trump
While tomorrow is election day, early voting has already seen a record 54 million people cast ballots around the country, reflecting the intense political fervor.
Trump’s second term has featured a relentless expansion of presidential power, aided by an ever-more docile Republican Party.

Trump has torn down part of the White House to build a ballroom, put his image on money and official buildings, disrupted the global economy with sweeping economic tariffs, and threatened to invade or annex allies like Canada and Greenland.
A big Democratic win would kick start the post-Trump era and could even begin the race to replace him in 2028.

Winning the House would put Democrats in charge of the federal budget and powerful committees set to probe allegations of mass corruption, Trump’s links to infamous sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, and other explosive topics.
The outcome of the contest for the Senate remains in doubt.

Only a third of the Senate’s 100 seats are being contested in these midterms and few of the races were seen as favorable to Democrats. However, with surprisingly strong challenges mounted in deeply Republican states like Texas and Kansas, pollsters now say the odds of a Democratic flip are at minimum even.
A Democratic Senate would be able to shut down Trump’s lifetime appointments to courts — especially the Supreme Court.
Will Trump accept results?
The midterms have seen about US$11 billion spent on advertising, with large chunks coming from individual mega-donors.
Elon Musk, a close Trump ally who led the so-called DOGE effort in dismantling entire government departments, has given a staggering nearly half-billion dollars to help get Republicans elected.
The campaigns have also been marked by blistering language and insults, led by Trump who falsely accused leading Democratic candidates of being everything from vegans to jihadists.
And hanging over everything is concern that Republicans will refuse to accept a loss, leading to a constitutional crisis similar to Trump’s attempt to overturn his 2020 presidential election defeat.
A federal judge on Sunday tossed out an extremely unusual attempt by Trump’s administration to hold up a potential victory by a Democratic candidate for Senate in Alaska.

The lawsuit contended that if Democrat Mary Peltola beats the Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan, the result should not be certified because there is a third, minor candidate also called Dan Sullivan, allegedly recruited by Democrats to siphon off votes. — AFP

84fe5f6538829b01: NOVEMBER 2 — Every time a climate report drops, the same ritual unfolds. Scientists issue grave warnings. Politicians trade soundbites. Corporations rebrand their logos in shades of green.

And the rest of us? We scroll past, overwhelmed, convinced that sustainability is a conversation for someone else — someone with a degree in environmental science, a seat at a policy table, or a budget line for carbon offsets.

This is a dangerous mistake. Public conversations on sustainability are not a luxury, a niche interest, or a distraction from “real” economic concerns. They are the foundation on which any meaningful change is built. And everyone — not just experts, activists, or executives — must invest in them.
Here is the uncomfortable truth: we already have most of the technology and policy tools we need to drastically reduce emissions, protect biodiversity, and build more resilient communities.
What we lack is collective will. And collective will does not emerge from white papers. It emerges from conversation.

When people talk about sustainability in everyday spaces — at kitchen tables, in classrooms, on factory floors, in faith communities, on social media — it stops being an abstract “issue” and becomes a shared reality. That shift matters.

Research consistently shows that people’s willingness to adopt sustainable behaviours is strongly influenced by what they believe others around them are doing. In other words, conversation is not just talk. It is infrastructure for change.

If ordinary people opt out of sustainability conversations, they don’t leave a vacuum. They leave a stage. And that stage gets filled by those with the most money, the most platforms, and the most to gain from the status quo.

We have seen this play out repeatedly. Fossil fuel companies have spent decades funding messaging that frames climate action as economic suicide. Greenwashing campaigns convince consumers that minor tweaks — a reusable straw here, a recycled tote there — are sufficient. Meanwhile, the structural changes that actually matter, such as transforming energy systems, rethinking urban planning, and reining in overconsumption, get pushed to the margins.
Public conversation is the antidote. It is how communities push back against spin, demand accountability, and insist that sustainability be treated as a matter of justice, not just branding.

There is a persistent myth that sustainability is a concern for the wealthy, the young, or the urban. In reality, it is the poor, the elderly, the rural, and the marginalised who suffer first and worst from environmental degradation. Farmers facing unpredictable seasons. Coastal communities facing rising seas. Workers in industries that must transition. Families breathing polluted air in cities that were never designed with their health in mind.

For these communities, sustainability is not a thought experiment. It is survival. Yet too often, they are the least represented in the conversations that shape policy. That is not just unjust; it is impractical. Solutions designed without the input of those most affected tend to fail.

Some will argue that they are too busy, too tired, or too disillusioned to engage. That is understandable. The problems are enormous, and individual action can feel futile. But opting out has a cost. When public conversation withers, so does public pressure. And when public pressure withers, governments and corporations feel free to delay, dilute, and distract.

We have seen what happens when sustainability is left to closed-door negotiations: ambitious targets get watered down, timelines slip, and vulnerable nations are left to fend for themselves. We cannot afford another decade of that.

Investing in public conversation does not mean everyone must become a climate activist or a policy wonk. It means something simpler and more accessible: Bring sustainability into your everyday conversations. Normalise it. Listen. Especially to those whose experiences differ from your own. Ask questions. Of your leaders, your employers, your neighbours, and yourself. Create space. In your workplace, your school, your place of worship, your community group. Refuse to let it be siloed.
Sustainability is not a separate topic. It is about food, housing, health, jobs, and justice.

The sustainability challenge is often framed as a series of trade-offs: economy versus environment, growth versus restraint, present versus future. But these framings assume that the conversation is a monologue delivered by experts to a passive public. It is not. It is a messy, vital, ongoing conversation among people who share a planet and a future.

That conversation will not be perfect. It will be uncomfortable. It will require humility, patience, and a willingness to change our minds. But it is the only way we move from awareness to action, from individual gestures to systemic change. Sustainability is not a topic. It is our shared life, and the conversation about it belongs to all of us.

edf377cdc391b618: NEW YORK, Nov 2 — Sweden’s Andreas Almgren won the New York City Marathon, clocking 2hr 6min 1sec in a spectacular debut at the distance yesterday.

The 31-year-old Almgren, in the spotlight after setting a European half-marathon record in Copenhagen in September, powered through the final mile to capture the victory over Italian Yemaneberhan Crippa.
Kenyan Sheila Chepkirui won the women’s race for a second time, repelling the challenge of last year’s winner Hellen Obiri — who faded to finish third behind American Jessica McClain.

Almgren, who won his first international athletics title in August with 10,000m gold at the European Championships, ran comfortably in a large lead group that also included defending champion Benson Kipruto.
He broke away in the final mile, pulling away from Crippa who finished second in 2:06:14.

Lesotho’s Kamohelo Mofolo was third in 2:06:26, narrowly holding off Kenya’s Kipruto — who had been trying to become the first back-to-back New York men’s winner since compatriot Geoffrey Mutai in 2013.
“I mean, you can’t ask for a better debut,” Almgren, draped in a Swedish flag in the sunshine of Central Park, told ESPN.
“I don’t know what to say. I just feel like I’m about to start crying,” he added after becoming the first Swede to win a major marathon.
“When Benson started picking up the pace with (five kilometers) left, I just felt like I’ve got the legs today.”
For Chepkirui, who won in 2:24:36, it wasn’t the first time she had dashed Obiri’s dreams of successive wins.
In 2024 she edged then-defending champion Obiri on the streets of the Big Apple.
It looked like it would again come down to the two of them as they powered together through the final mile, Chepkirui doggedly defending her place in front.
- ‘Really tricky’ -
“The last mile was really tricky,” Chepkirui said. “I had to be patient because I knew Hellen was really strong, so I have to really push up to the finish line.”
As she did, McClain squeezed past Obiri to take second in 2:24:42, Obiri settling for third in 2:24:43.
“I don’t think I have the words yet,” McClain said after becoming the first US woman since 2018 to finish on the podium.

“I honestly didn’t feel amazing through like 18 (miles), just kind of had to stick in it and adjust. Top five was top of mind, then podium. I was, like, just stick with it, and all of a sudden Hellen was coming back to me and I don’t really know what happened.”
The race marked the 50th anniversary of the current incarnation of the NYC Marathon, which links the city’s five boroughs of Staten Island, Brooklyn, Queens, the Bronx, and Manhattan.
The race was first run in 1970 when the course was confined to Central Park, becoming a city-wide event in 1976.
Switzerland’s world record-holder Catherine Debrunner, the 2023 women’s wheelchair winner, crushed the field for her second New York victory in 1:40:02.

Her compatriot Marcel Hug, the men’s world record-holder, claimed his eighth New York wheelchair title, holding off Daniel Romanchuk in a sprint finish to win in 1:28:14 - 1.13 seconds in front of the American. — AFP
